#1903. Arsenal set price for Chelsea to sign Martin Zubimendi after Real Madrid approach

Chelsea have revived their interest in Arsenal midfielder Martin Zubimendi ahead of the January transfer window but face competition from Real Madrid and Atletico Madrid.

The Blues were one of a number of clubs to express interest in signing Zubimendi last summer but the Spanish World Cup winner ended up staying at Arsenal.

Zubimendi enjoyed a bright start to his Arsenal career following a £60m move from Real Sociedad in 2025 but became a less influential figure in Mikel Arteta’s side towards the end of last season.

The 27-year-old appeared fatigued in the second-half of the campaign and lost his place in the team, with a then 19-year-old Myles Lewis-Skelly starting the Champions League final ahead of him.

Zubimendi saw the intense competition for places at the Emirates Stadium only increase in the summer as Arsenal spent £75m to sign Brazilian midfielder Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle United.

As a result Zubimendi is still waiting for his first Premier League start of the season, with his lack of game-time sparking renewed speculation over his future in north London.

Zubimendi’s frustrating spell at Arsenal has not put off potential suitors, with Chelsea, Real Madrid and Atletico Madrid all ‘monitoring’ the Spaniard ahead of the January transfer window.

According to The Independent, all three clubs suspect a January deal could be possible and view Zubimendi as an ideal acquisition given he is now a Premier League, World Cup, European Championship and Nations League winner.

But Arsenal’s desire to sign a new forward in January may depend on a major sale and Zubimendi would be an obvious candidate to be moved on, although the English champions would want to recoup at least the £60m they paid for him 16 months ago.

Jose Mourinho also intends to sign a new midfielder in January and Real Madrid have been huge admirers of Zubimendi ever since he broke through in La Liga.

But Real face competition from arch-rivals Atletico, with reports in Spain claiming Diego Simeone is ‘dreaming’ of signing Zubimendi from Arsenal.

Zubimendi came on as an injury-time substitute in Arsenal’s 1-0 win over Hull City on Saturday, a result that sent Arteta’s side six points clear at the top of the table.

#1902. Cisse like the greats, Amorim surpasses Allegri: All the key stats from Genoa 1-2 AC Milan

AC Milan won their seventh Serie A game of the season on Sunday afternoon, beating a Genoa side that entered the game in great form.

The home crowd at the Marassi were fired up going into this one given Genoa had won four of their last five. However, goals from Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic inside the opening 20 minutes was exactly what Milan needed to take the ascendancy.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Ellertsson did score inside the final few minutes as Genoa mounted a late surge in the hopes of snatching a point, but the Rossoneri held on to win 2-1 and move back into the top four places in the table.

Looking at the general stats makes for interesting reading. Milan dominated the ball with 62% possession, but Genoa had nearly double the Expected Goals (1.14 to 0.61), even though big chances ended up being even at two apiece.

The Rossoblu also had nearly triple the shots (17 to 6) and shots on target (5 to 2), while the Rossoneri did not win a single corner. It suggests that Ruben Amorim’s side simply took their moments and sat back, though maybe Daniele De Rossi can feel a bit hard done by.

📊 The stats from the win against Genoa. pic.twitter.com/wr1E6cohcZ

— MilanData📊 (@acmilandata) November 8, 2026

Alphadjo Cisse is one of only three players born in 2006 or later to have scored 8+ goals across all competitions in Europe’s top five leagues. The others are Lamine Yamal (13) and Paris Brunner (8).

In terms of minutes per goal in Serie A, Cisse leads the way with one every 81 minutes. That puts him ahead of the likes of Donyell Malen (one every 82), Lautaro Martinez (one every 88) and Gustavo Varela (one every 91).

After 13 appearances for Milan, Cisse is level with Filippo Inzaghi, Andriy Shevchenko and Alberto Gilardino on 8 goals. Pierino Prati (10) and Mario Balotelli (12) are the only players to record more.

Milan are unbeaten in their last 11 Serie A matches against Genoa (W7, D4). Since 2020-21, the Rossoneri only have a longer run of unbeaten games against Hellas Verona (12).

The Diavolo have won each of their last five Serie A away games against Genoa. Only against one team do the Rossoneri currently have a longer running away win streak in the competition: Hellas Verona (seven).

Milan have won three and drawn three of their first six away games this season. The Rossoneri have pnly avoided defeat in their first six away games of the season on three occasions between 2020-21 and 2025-26, the same number as Inter and Napoli, and could now become the only team to do so four times in this span, including the current season.

With this victory, AC Milan climbed to 24 points in the standings, two more than the number earned by Massimiliano Allegri’s Milan last season after 11 games. This is also better than Stefano Pioli’s last season, also by two points.

#1901. Chelsea handed midfielder suspension boost after squad announcement

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Chelsea have been handed an unexpected boost, with Romeo Lavia set to serve a suspension for Belgium.

Following an absence of more than three years, Lavia returned to the Belgium squad for the extended autumn international break and featured in all four Nations League fixtures.

While the 22-year-old was unable to complete 90 minutes during the Nations League quadruple-header, he did play 85 and 87 minutes respectively during his two starts against France.

However, there were concerns over his fitness upon being substituted in the first of those meetings - though Belgium head coach Mark van Bommel was quick to allay any such fears of a fresh injury setback.

"Romeo came on as a substitute against Italy and played 85 minutes against France,” Van Bommel explained.

“He did a fantastic job. You can already assume that I won't be starting him.

“Chelsea are being cautious with him, and so are we. We want to make optimal use of his qualities.”

In Belgium’s two victories - over Italy and Belgium - Lavia came off the bench in both, though being shown a yellow card in the opening game of the international break left him walking the disciplinary tight-rope for the remaining three games.

As per article 60 of the ‘Regulations of the UEFA Nations League’ handbook explaining yellow and red cards, the ruling states: ‘During the league phase, players and team officials are suspended for the next competition match after two yellow cards and any subsequent even-numbered yellow card (e.g. fourth, sixth).’

As Lavia was booked against France to double his yellow card count, it means he will be suspended for Belgium’s next Nations League match against Turkey on November 12.

As Lavia has been named in the Belgium squad for this month’s internationals, he is only available for selection against Italy on November 15 which should serve as a boost for Chelsea and Xabi Alonso.

The midfielder’s injury issues in the past are well documented, but has largely managed to stay fit all season, making 10 appearances across all competitions.

#1900. Rio Ferdinand names his top choice to replace Michael Carrick at Manchester United

Rio Ferdinand says Mauricio Pochettino is the candidate who ‘jumps off the list’ to replace Michael Carrick at Manchester United.

Carrick, 45, looks set to be sacked following United’s disastrous start to the 2026/27 campaign.

Manchester United are 18th in the Premier League going into the November international break, just one point off bottom spot.

Old Trafford bosses are currently reviewing Carrick’s position but a change in the dugout appears to be the most likely outcome.

Eddie Howe, Fabian Hurzeler, Julian Nagelsmann and Antonio Conte have all been linked with Manchester United over the past couple of months.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Pochettino has also emerged as a candidate to replace Carrick and Ferdinand has put his support behind the Argentine.

Pochettino, 54, signed an extension to his contract as USA coach after last summer’s World Cup but the deal is believed to contain a release clause.

‘People are talking about Mauricio Pochettino and it looks like he’s at the front of the queue right now,’ Ferdinand said on his YouTube channel.

‘We spent some time with him and his team in the summer, they’re really good guys and competent at what they do.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘I look at Pochettino and one of his biggest assets is that human element of his management and building confidence with his players. That’s a big part of Manchester United at the moment because we’ve got far too many broken individuals.

‘How that gets rebuilt, is that coaching, results or somebody coming in and putting an arm around their shoulder? It’s going to be all of that.

‘I look at that group of names and think Pochettino is the one that jumps off the list as someone who has more of the things we’re looking for to save and build a group of players.

‘I think he’s got more than the others from what I’ve seen and my interactions with him over time.

‘There’s not many names jumping off the page when you look at it. People will say, “what has Pochettino won?”, but you can say the same about Eddie Howe.

‘The standards have dropped massively so let’s be realistic about where we are. There’s a process to get back there. We need to stabilise and get back in the Champions League again.’

Pochettino began his managerial career at Espanyol before his prominence rose during a short but impressive spell in charge of Southampton.

He then spent five years at Tottenham, taking Spurs to the final of both the Champions League and Carabao Cup but failing to win a trophy in north London.

Pochettino had mixed stints at PSG and Chelsea before taking over as coach of the United States in September 2024.

His USA team impressed in the group stages of last summer’s World Cup, topping Group D, but suffered a humbling 4-1 defeat to Belgium in the last-16.

Manchester United’s first game after the international break is a daunting trip to Anfield to face arch-rivals Liverpool on November 22.

#1898. New Zealand vs India - prediction, team news, lineups

By Anthony Nolan | 11 Nov 2026 02:09, Last updated: 11 Nov 2026 05:00

India are set for a tough test on Thursday, when they travel to Auckland's Go Media Stadium for an international friendly against New Zealand, marking their first-ever visit to the country.

The All Whites are hoping to bounce back from defeat last time out, while the Blue Tigers are looking to follow the winning example set by their alternative squad at the SAFF Championship.

Darren Bazeley's New Zealand followed up their group-stage elimination from World Cup 2026 with a three-game unbeaten run, drawing 2-2 with Palestine before triumphing 3-0 against China and on penalties against Panama during the last international break.

However, the All Whites' streak came to an end on October 5, when they were downed 2-1 by Japan in the final of the friendly Kirin Cup.

Captain Chris Wood - the nation's record scorer and appearance holder - assisted Ben Old's equaliser that day, but he was unable to respond when Ritsu Doan netted the winner for the Samurai Blue four minutes after his second-half substitution.

Looking ahead to Thursday, the hosts have never lost to India, most recently running out 2-1 winners in the friendly AIFF Intercontinental Cup in June 2018.

However, this week's clash will be just the second time they have faced the visitors this century, and only the third meeting between the sides throughout history, after first locking horns during a goalless draw in the 1981 edition of the Merdeka Tournament.

New Zealand (ranked 88th) are the favourites to come out on top due to their 50-superior placement in FIFA's ranking system, though fans may still be cautious considering that Bazeley's team have lost two of their last three matches on home turf.

Meanwhile, Khalid Jamil's India arrive as underdogs but are keen to test their mettle in a pair of fixtures against an opponent who qualified for the World Cup.

Thursday's friendly in Auckland and Sunday's follow up in Christchurch come as part of a celebration marking 100 years of sporting connection between the nations, and the Blue Tigers' manager called for fans to join them on matchday in his press conference.

“I know there are many Indian fans here in New Zealand - I would request them to come to the stadium and support the team. Their support is important for us, and we will try to give our best on the pitch,” said Jamil.

Another challenge facing the visitors is the fact they are split across two squads, one that is set to take part in these friendlies and another that is currently contesting the 2026 SAFF Championship, the latter of which beat Pakistan 3-2 on November 5.

Beyond that victory by their alternative side, India are heading into this clash on the back of a seven-game winless run in friendlies, including a 6-1 thrashing by Uruguay and a 4-0 hammering by Brazil last month.

New Zealand International Friendlies form:

New Zealand are without right-back Callan Elliot through injury, but the versatile Bill Tuiloma could feature in his absence, joining Nando Pijnaker, Tyler Bindon and James McGarry in defence.

At the opposite end of the pitch, Chris Wood looks set to lead the line, supported from out wide by Dundee United's Jesse Randall and 20-year-old Nathan Walker of Wellington Phoenix, who could make his All Whites debut.

As for India, they have left experienced goalkeeper Gurpreet Singh Sandhu out of the squad, while centre-back Anwar Ali is sidelined due to a hamstring injury.

With that in mind, Vishal Kaith is likely to start between the sticks on Thursday, shielded by a pairing of Bijoy Varghese and Mehtab Singh.

The Blue Tigers are also without midfielder Lalengmawia Ralte, who is known as Apuia, though Anirudh Thapa could be joined by Lalrinliana Hnamte in the visitors' double pivot.

Paulsen; Tuiloma, Pijnaker, Bindon, McGarry; Rufer; Randall, Garbett, Bayliss, Walker; Wood

Kaith; Singh Tekcham, Varghese, Me Singh, Mishra; Hnamte, Thapa; Ma Singh, Williams, Kuruniyan; Lalhlansanga

New Zealand are the overwhelming favourites despite featuring a number of young players in their squad, and they will be hoping to deliver a strong showing on home soil.

India will arrive knowing that they are likely to be on the losing side, but that underdog status could inspire them to find the back of the net at least once on Thursday.

#1897. Harry Kane names two players who can break his England record ahead of special night

Harry Kane has named two England players he believes might be able to break his caps record — but first hopes to reach a tally of appearances they cannot match.

Kane will overtake Peter Shilton to become the all-time most-capped player for the national team on Thursday when he earns his 126th appearance by leading England out against Croatia in the Nations League.

Kane is also the all-time record scorer with 91 England goals, and the Ballon d’Or winner says he will set his sights on reaching 100 England goals once he has overtaken Shilton to claim the caps record for himself.

The 77-year-old former goalkeeper will be involved in a commemoration for Kane before kick-off at Wembley on Thursday.

Kane, though, insists it is his nature to “always look forward” and is hoping he can reach a number of England appearances that is so high that key midfielders Jude Bellingham - who has 60 caps - and Declan Rice - who has 80 - in particular are never able to match him.

“Look at Jude or Dec, for example — they’re on 60-odd caps already,” Kane said. “And look at how young they are. I will try and give them a good number to catch.

“The goal record is going to be one that is going to be difficult to beat for a while [after me].”

The England captain, who was last month crowned winner of the Ballon d’Or at the age of 33, says he will always feel he has a “point to prove”, adding that he feels no need to be a “show off” and that just because he does not have the “ego” of some of the “great players”, does not mean he “doesn’t want it as much”.

Kane also holds the record for England appearances as captain, having overtaken Billy Wright and Bobby Moore who shared the record for decades with 90 caps as captain each.

Kane has earned 75 per cent of his England appearances as the skipper.

“That is something I didn’t really take in,” he said. “I was talking to Michael Olise at Bayern and asking how old he was.

“He said 23 at the time and I said: ‘Jeez, I was [England] captain by then’. I don’t think I realised how young I was at the time.

‘Maybe he can do a little bit better. Alright, that’s part of it, he’s made a mistake. But he cares an awful lot, and he’s given everything.

‘So I like what he brings to the team. I like what he brings to the group. I like what he brings to the whole environment and the culture that we’ve got.

‘Picking the team and who plays the next game, that’s a whole different decision. But it’s a whole different game that we’ve got to look forward to now.’

An eighth league game without a win leaves Manchester United 18th in the Premier League going into the November international break.

A dismal start to the 2026/27 campaign looks set to cost Carrick his job at Old Trafford, with Eddie Howe the current frontrunner to take over.

#1894. USA release training footage as Mauricio Pochettino sends message amid Manchester United links

Mauricio Pochettino took USMNT training on Wednesday as usual, despite reports of an agreement being in place with Manchester United.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea head coach is widely expected to make a surprise return to English football, just over two years after his last stint in the Premier League.

Over the weekend, and following Man United’s 4-4 draw at home to Aston Villa, Pochettino emerged as the new favourite to replace Michael Carrick should the current United head coach be sacked.

And there have been been big developments since. Most notably a report from the Athletic who state United spent Tuesday discussing personal terms with Pochettino’s representatives, with no major obstacles expected and that a final agreement is expected.

However, it should be noted that United have yet to approach US Soccer, who would be entitled to around $10m (£7.4m) in compensation through an exit clause in the Argentine’s contract as manager of the national team.

In the meantime, it was business as usual for Pochettino on Wednesday as he oversaw a training session in preparation for USA’s CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final tie first leg against Haiti.

This comes after USA cancelled their media access day in observance of Veterans Day, thus removing the possibility of the squad being asked to comment on the news of Pochettino’s potential exit.

On X, formerly, Twitter, the official USMNT account has uploaded footage of the aforementioned training session with Pochettino sending a message to his players before putting them through their paces.

Pochettino is due to address reporters on Friday in the pre-match press conference, where he will be expected to field questions about his future - especially if there has been no further movement with Man United.

#1893. Sky: Ramos involved but has minimal support – the numbers that illustrate Amorim’s point

Some interesting analysis on AC Milan and Goncalo Ramos’ attacking struggles has been provided by the Sky studios.

It was a familiar tale for Ramos during Milan’s 2-1 win over Genoa on Sunday. He was involved but rarely inside the box, then he was selfless instead of ruthless in front of goal when he chose to square for Christian Pulisic to make it 2-0.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The worries are starting to grow regarding whether the Portuguese can provide the output required of a number nine that cost €70m. Yet, the Rossoneri have scored 23 goals in 11 league games which suggests goals are coming from elsewhere, sometimes with Ramos’ help.

Sky offered some interesting insight after Sunday’s game. Firstly, they picked out just how involved Ramos actually is with various aspects of Milan’s overall play.

For example, he is first among Serie A strikers for interceptions and recoveries, while he is second for receptions, touches and duels. He is third for passes.

He is first among centre-forwards in the league for touches in the middle third of the field and touches in the opposition half. He is second for fouls committed plus fouls suffered among forwards, with 41.

Sky then shift the focus to the team’s overall play to try and explain why Ramos perhaps isn’t getting the quality service and is having to drop deeper as a result.

They look at data per 30 minutes of possession. Milan are first in Serie A for build-up actions, but they are 20th for entries into the final third and entries into the opposition box.

Amorim’s side are 19th for percentage of touches in the attacking third and 18th in percentage of touches in the opposition box. With numbers like these, there isn’t much for Ramos to get on the end of.

What does this tell us? Well, Amorim’s post match assessment about struggling to get the ball from the defensive third into the final third are true. Milan have a lot of the ball but still struggle to progress it, as the coach told Sky.

“I think it’s difficult for a striker when he doesn’t score goals. But I’ll repeat: we don’t spend much time in the final third of the pitch. We have possession, we’re improving our ball output, but we’re missing that. When we’re consistently in the final third, Gonçalo will score a lot of goals,” he said.

“It’s a team problem, we’re not helping Ramos, but he’s helping us a lot. It’s a process, a journey. And we’re not yet at the point of being so dominant that Ramos spends most of his time in the opponent’s penalty area. We’re still a long way off.”

#1892. Guatemala vs Canada - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joel Lefevre | 11 Nov 2026 02:46

Making their first appearance in the quarter-finals of the CONCACAF Nations League, Guatemala will host Canada in the opening leg of that tie on Friday at Estadio El Trebol in Guatemala City.

A 1-0 win over Suriname helped the Guatemalans top Group B with seven points, while Canada are one of the top four ranked teams in CONCACAF, earning a bye into the knockout stage as a result.

It was a roller coaster of a group stage for Guatemala, but fortunately for them it ended with the Central Americans at the top.

Luis Fernando Tena’s men opened that phase by conceding an injury-time goal in a defeat to Jamaica (3-2) but ended it with an stoppage-time winner versus Suriname.

That victory vaulted them into the Nations League knockout stage for the first time, scoring nine goals along the way, the joint-most for them ever in the League A group phase.

Unfortunately though it came at a cost as the coach will be missing some players for this match due to the post-match altercations in that outing.

Since their heartbreaking defeat on matchday one to the Jamaicans, Guatemala have collected a clean sheet in their last three Nations League affairs, having conceded a combined 14 goals this year before this tournament began.

In their six previous League A encounters at home, this team have yet to lose, while conceding a mere two goals overall during that stretch.

Los Chapines can stretch their unbeaten run against Canada to three matches across all competitions, eliminating them on penalties in the 2025 CONCACAF Gold Cup quarter-finals.

Following their historic run to the last 16 of the World Cup last summer, the Canadians had a solid fall international window.

Jesse Marsch’s men won two of their three friendlies in that window, collecting two clean sheets along the way.

On Friday, they will hope to avoid consecutive international defeats for the first time since the 2024 Copa America, after losing their last international outing to the USA (1-0).

The Canucks boast a 100% away record in the quarter-finals of this tournament, winning at Jamaica in 2023 (2-1) and blanking Suriname on the road a year later (1-0).

They have won their last four internationals when netting the opening goal and have never lost a knockout match in this competition as the visiting team.

Friday will be their second Nations League match on Central American soil, with Les Rouges losing the previous one in the group stage at Honduras in 2022 (2-1).

Because of a post-match confrontation against Suriname, Jonathan Franco and Carlos Estrada will be suspended for three matches, while Oscar Santis is out due to a hamstring strain.

Matt Evans netted in the 96th minute to earn them a place in the knockout stage of this competition, his first goal on the international stage, and Nicholas Hagen collected two clean sheets in the group phase.

Canadian captain Alphonso Davies is reportedly ready to play according to Marsch, though Jonathan Osorio and Jacob Shaffelburg withdrew with injuries, while Cyle Larin was not selected because of back irritation.

Davies can move into a tie for ninth in all-time international goals Friday, while Richie Laryea will draw even with Paul Stalteri for sixth in all-time caps with his next one.

Hagen; Herrera, Yanes, Samayoa, Morales; Lopez, Castellanos, Rosales, Escobar, Rubin, Lom

Crepeau; Laryea, De Fougeroles, Ivanisevic, Davies; Buchanan, Saliba, Choiniere, Millar; J. David, Oluwaseyi

Even with Davies back, the environment in Guatemala will be difficult for the visitors to navigate, and we expect the Central Americans’ suffocating defence to limit the scoring chances for Canada.

William Gallas believes that only one team has the ability to rival Arsenal in this season’s Premier League title race.

Arsenal are now five points clear at the top of the league table following their hard-fought 1-0 win at home to Hull City on Saturday.

But it was another bad weekend for Manchester City as their third successive league defeat saw Enzo Maresca’s side slip to third.

Brighton are now second in the table as Fabian Hurzeler’s side continued their superb start to the season with a 2-0 win over Brentford.

#1890. 'This club's not used to losing' - keeper Johnstone opens up on Celtic struggles

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 13:00 EST, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 13:48 EST, 7 November 2026

Sam Johnstone has warned that Thursday's dramatic win over Besiktas must be seen as just the first step on Celtic's road to recovery.

The pulsating 3-2 triumph over the Turks came after Martin O'Neill's men had lost four straight matches in Europe with just three wins in the previous ten matches in all competitions.

As timely as the result was, the keeper believes there's a lot of hard work for the side to get through before anyone can talk about it being a turning point in what's been a trying season to this stage.

Asked if the spirit in the camp had been affected by a string of adverse results, Johnstone said: 'Of course it has. I think the results affect it.

'This club's not used to losing and we've probably lost too many games for this club.

'We all realise that, but we have to put things right in each game.

'The lads go out to win every game, so the camp's good.

'It was tough. We're honest players, we're honest people and honest with each other.

'You could see on Thursday night that the lads put a good fight in and got the result.'

Signed on loan from Wolves for the season, Johnstone was handed his chance by O'Neill only to drop out of the team following an indifferent display in the 3-0 loss at Ibrox on September 13.

Celtic goalkeeper is finding his feet in Scottish football after a difficult start

But having been selected ahead of Viljami Sinisalo in the past five matches, the former England goalkeeper believes he's steadily making progress.

'To get a run of games for any player, you find your rhythm,' Johnstone explained.

'It was a new club for me, a new team, so that takes probably a couple of games to get used to as well.

'I think I've got to get used to them (defenders), they've got to get used to me and that only happens through playing and through games. It's great to be in the team.

'It's good. I love playing. It's a great team to play in, a great club to play for and we keep taking it game by game. We go again on Sunday.'

Johnstone moved to Celtic at the start of a difficult period which saw the side struggle for consistency.

Adamant that he's never regretted moving up to Scotland for a minute, however, he added: 'The expectation, rightly so, for this place is to win games.

'Unfortunately, we hadn't quite met that expectation and the lads know that.

'Like I said, we try to win every game and put things right.

Celtic fought back for a much-needed Europa League victory against Besiktas

'It's brilliant to play for this club. The passion of the fans, good and bad. The standard of players on the pitch, day in, day out at training.

'When I came, I said I didn't have to think twice about coming here.'

Having heard so much about Celtic Park on the night of a big European win, the keeper was glad to finally witness it for himself.

'It was unbelievable to experience this place, rocking and get the win,' he reflected.

'It's a great feeling. It's great to play in front of and feel the passion of the fans. That does help the lads and drives the lads on.

'As you could see, there were times in the game where we struggled a little bit, but the lads dug in. It's never going to be easy.

'In the Europa League, you're playing top teams and, after last week's result as well, we were under a lot of pressure. The lads came up with the goods.

'We've still got a chance to qualify, and that's our aim, so we'll take the next game the same as any other game, that we go to win.'

#1889. Martin Zubimendi responds to Chelsea transfer speculation and reveals Mikel Arteta warning

Martin Zubimend has revealed he was warned he would face a fight to maintain his status as a regular starter at Arsenal this season, but insists he hasn’t given up hope of winning back his place.

The Spain international joined the Gunners 18 months ago following a £60million move from Real Sociedad.

Zubimendi had come close to signing for Liverpool a year earlier, but was convinced to snub the Reds’ interest and delay a move to England, with Mikel Arteta outlining his determination to make him a key component of his midfield rebuild.

The 27-year-old’s decision to move to the north London club initially looked an inspired one as he played almost every game over the course of the first two thirds of a campaign that ultimately ended in glory.

Fatigue, however, eventually caught up with Zubimendi and his place was effectively taken by teenager Myles Lewis-Skelly during the run-in and he has been reduced to a bit-part role ever since.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Arsenal’s decision to sanction the signing of Bruno Guimaraes has only served to further heighten the intense competition for places and, as a result, Zubimendi is yet to start a Premier League game this season.

That lack of game time has sparked intense speculation that a January move could be on the cards for the World Cup winner.

Chelsea, who are in the market for a midfielder and whose manager, Xabi Alonso, attempted to sign Zubimendi during his brief stint in charge of Real Madrid, are said to be considering renewing interest having made tentative enquiries during the summer.

Atletico Madrid, meanwhile, have been positioned as the frontrunners, with Diego Simeone said to be dreaming of signing the Arsenal star with reports in Spain going as far as saying that a deal is close.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Responding to a whirlwind of rumours, Zubimendi told Marca: ‘To be honest, I’m sometimes surprised by the press too. I understand that the winter transfer window is approaching and rumors can surface, but I think we need to be a bit more careful with what we publish.

‘Ultimately, everyone has a team they play for, and we need to respect that. I’ve also read that I might be close, but not at all.

‘Often a news story comes out and it seems that if it doesn’t come true, it’s quickly forgotten and nothing happens. I’m learning how this world works and getting used to it, but sometimes I could avoid a lot of the messages I receive because of this kind of news.’

Asked whether his current predicament has come as a surprise, Zubimendi revealed Arteta had been totally transparent at the season’s outset and outlined the role he envisaged for a player he fought so hard to sign.

He said:  ‘I spoke with Mikel at the beginning of the season. As he does with all the players, he explained the plan to me.

‘He warned me that there were new signings and that there would be playing time for everyone. And here we are, fighting for it.

‘I understand because, for me, we’re among the five best teams in Europe. There are some fantastic players. New signings have arrived in my position, and there were already some very good players. I’m also part of that competition that makes it so difficult to get playing time.’

He added:  ‘I’m calm and happy with how I’m handling this situation. It’s something I’ve never experienced before, and I think you learn from these situations too.

‘Besides, it’s in moments like these that you need the people around you the most, and they’re there for you.

‘I’m patient. When you’ve been playing a lot of minutes and your role changes to not playing as much, I’m able to see the positive side. I think everything passes, that just like last year the opposite happened to me and I played practically everything, this can change very quickly.’

By Axel Clody | 11 Nov 2026 06:57, Last updated: 11 Nov 2026 06:57

Endrick is expected to leave Real Madrid again in the January transfer window. A Champions League club has been installed as favourites to land him.

Seven matches played, a single start, one goal and one assist: that is Endrick’s statistical record in the start of this season at Real Madrid.

After a successful loan at Lyon in the second half of last season, the Brazilian striker returned to Real Madrid, but the competition in attack is too great. A departure seems increasingly likely.

Currently, less than two months before the January transfer window opens, the Real Madrid player is preparing his departure and looking for a new destination.

A rebound like the one offered by Lyon last winter is being sought, where he would have guaranteed playing time and the chance to play European matches.

Roma are interested in Endrick’s profile, but Sporting represent a formidable competitor in this race. The Portuguese club have already positioned themselves to sign the Brazilian in the second half of the season.

It should be noted that the striker, who is also on Arsenal’s shortlist, has not yet made a decision and has not ruled out leaving on a permanent transfer, which would guarantee Real Madrid retained control over his future, either through a buy-back clause or the sale of part of his rights.

Manchester United are close to rubber stamping a deal to appoint Michael Carrick’s successor ahead of making a final decision on the future of their current head coach.

United are understood to have been in contact with Pochettino’s representatives and although personal terms are unlikely to be an issue, the 54-year-old’s exit clause of £7.4million would need to be paid in full.

Carrick’s side subsequently lost 2-0 at Chelsea, where they were unable to take their chances and saw Lisandro Martinez sent off, before last Tuesday’s thrilling 3-2 Champions League comeback win against Roma.

A scarcely believable 4-4 draw against followed on Sunday, after which the head coach stressed he would not walk away.

‘It’s been a right mixed week or two or three, really, if you’re looking at the events,’ Carrick said. ‘But I’m pretty clear where we need to go and how we need to get there.

‘Obviously some of the boys will be flying off around the world and different things, and the group will be split for 10 days or so.

‘But as a normal international week is, you know, we’ll have some training. We’ll have one or two days off, but not too much. But we’ll train, and we’ll get ready for the next game.’

United return to action with a Premier League trip to rivals Liverpool on November 22.

#1882. Danny Murphy tells Liverpool to explore transfer move for £33m Man Utd target

Danny Murphy has urged Liverpool to strongly consider a transfer move for Barcelona misfit Alejandro Balde this winter.

Liverpool invested heavily in the summer with a view to giving Andoni Iraola the best possible chance in the hot seat following Arne Slot’s dismissal as manager.

It saw Jeremy Jacquet, Bradley Barcola and Victor Munoz all added to Iraola’s squad for a combined fee of around £200million – and the trio have gone on to enjoy encouraging starts to life at Anfield.

With the Reds having dropped points in five of their opening ten matches of the Premier League campaign, though, attentions have quickly turned to the January transfer window as an opportunity to further strengthen.

Milos Kerkez has blown hot and cold since joining Liverpool for a fee of £40million from Bournemouth 18 months ago and rumours have been circulating that the club could reenter the transfer market for a new left-back.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

The Merseyside giants have been credited with a strong interest in Juventus’ Andrea Cambiaso and Santos’ Vinicius Lira in recent days, with Kerkez and Kostas Tsimikas both yet to fully convince fans that they could eventually fill the shoes left by Andy Robertson.

But according to Murphy, ‘super talent’ Balde could be the ideal signing for Liverpool given the out-of-favour Spaniard is already used to the expectations that come with playing for a ‘huge football club’.

Balde has made just three substitute appearances for Barca in La Liga this term and Manchester United have also been named as a potential escape route for the £33m-rated defender at the halfway point of the season.

‘I think Liverpool will be looking for a left-back but it’s hard because I don’t know Kerkez personally, I know he’s trying really hard and you can see it in his energy that he cares, and that’s a great start,’ the ex-Liverpool and England midfielder told Betarades.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘He cares for the shirt and he’s working really hard to try and make it happen.

‘I think Balde could be great for Liverpool because he’s a super talent and he’s also got that experience of being at a huge football club with that expectation.

‘Balde’s a really good player. There’s lots of good players out there and Liverpool will be scouring the world.’

Murphy believes it could be time for Liverpool to look for ‘more established’ and ‘ready-made players’ after prioritising youth in recent transfer windows.

‘I think the most important thing is trying to bring somebody in who doesn’t make you guess whether he can deal with the pressure of a big club,’ he added.

‘It’s a delicate balance because Liverpool for years were very good at taking diamonds in from the rough, if you like. Someone like [Philippe] Coutinho, like [Andy] Robertson, like [Sadio] Mane even from Southampton. [Roberto] Firmino was about £20m.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

‘Liverpool took those diamonds in the rough and moulded them into these superstars, and then when we’ve tried to go and spend massive money on these already made stars, it’s not quite worked.

‘I still think there are times, especially in defensive areas where you really do want ready-made players. Especially when you’re struggling.

‘I think Liverpool have got enough young players now who need to grow. I think now there’s an argument to have a few more players who are maybe a bit more established.’

Murphy has some sympathy for Kerkez but feels the Hungary international needs to get his head down and work on his composure if he is to make a success of his time at Liverpool.

‘He just lacks composure and quality in the final third when he gets there. Too often his final pass or his cross isn’t good enough,’ he continued.

‘He doesn’t have the composure of an Andy Robertson, and to be fair to him, you are filling the boots of arguably one of the best left-backs Liverpool’s ever had.”

‘I think the lack of quality at times is due to the fact he’s very fast. He’s very much 100 miles an hour. I’m surprised they’re not working with him more to slow him down in those areas and to just calm himself.

‘Now it wouldn’t be as bad if he was brilliant defensively, but he’s struggling defensively as well. His positional play is sometimes a bit off, he’s a bit erratic in terms of diving in or getting beat.

‘He likes jumping into people. It’s a dilemma for Liverpool, and I think one that they’ll definitely be looking at and trying to address, because not every signing works out.’

On Kerkez, Murphy went on: ‘I was somebody who saw him that year at Bournemouth and thought he looked like a terrific young player.

‘But the one thing that people don’t understand and it’s only when you’ve been in that position you can empathise with going from playing in one environment to being in the intense, magnified world of Liverpool Football Club.

‘Every game, every minute, every mistake is analysed by the fans, by the press, by the worldwide audience, and I think that expectation, and that pressure is a bit much for him.’

#1881. Who can England face in Nations League quarter-final? Next opponents confirmed ahead of Croatia rematch

England are on course to record their best ever performance in the Nations League, having beaten the Czech Republic twice and Croatia during the autumn international break.

Including its inaugural season in 2018/19, the Three Lions have competed in every single Nations League campaign, experiencing some highs and the lowest of lows.

From topping their group and qualifying for the Nations League finals and finishing third to suffering a shock relegation in 2022/23 and then immediate promotion, England have done almost everything except win the competition.

Having started the 2026/27 campaign with a loss to Spain, despite leading 2-1 at one stage, England bounced back in style by beating the Czechs twice and then thumping Croatia 7-0 to put themselves in a great position to advance to the quarter-finals.

Whether that be as group winners or runners-up will ultimately be determined during this international break, but Thomas Tuchel’s side have positioned themselves well to qualify for the Nations League knockout stage with two games remaining.

The victory against Czech Republic at Wembley last month has practically guaranteed England a top-two finish in Nations League A, Group 3.

They are not technically into the knockout stages just yet, though, but mathematically, it is nigh-on impossible for Croatia to jump above them.

They would need to defeat the Three Lions by eight unanswered goals at Wembley on Thursday to stop Tuchel’s men progressing.

As such, England, six points clear of their rivals, can pretty much consider themselves qualified for the last eight.

The four group winners will face the four runners-up in a two-legged Nations League quarter-final.

The group winners will all be seeded and will have home advantage in their respective second leg ties. Teams from the same group cannot be paired together in the knockout stage, therefore England and Spain - for example - would be kept apart.

As things stand, if England finish second in Group 3, their potential Nations League quarter-final opponents would be France, Netherlands or Portugal.

Topping the group would set up a possible quarter-final showdown with Italy, Greece or Denmark.

The draw for the 2026/27 Nations League quarter-final will take place on Friday, November, 20 with the ties scheduled to take place in March 2027.

#1880. Man Utd next manager: What Antonio Conte has done in bid to beat Mauricio Pochettino to Old Trafford job

By Lewis Blain | 11 Nov 2026 07:17

Antonio Conte is making moves to strengthen his bid to become Manchester United's next manager, as uncertainty over Michael Carrick's future continues.

The ruthless Italian remains on United's shortlist alongside former Tottenham Hotspur boss Mauricio Pochettino, despite reservations within the club about appointing him.

With Carrick expected to leave in the coming days, Conte could now emerge as a serious contender for the imminent Old Trafford vacancy.

According to Foot Mercato journalist Santi Aouna, super-agent Pini Zahavi is representing Conte in discussions over the Red Devils job.

The 57-year-old is among the candidates being considered by the United hierarchy, with Zahavi potentially helping to position him for an appointment.

It's believed that Conte remains on the shortlist alongside Pochettino, although there are still some doubts within the club about whether the former Inter Milan, Chelsea and Spurs manager is the right fit.

However, with Carrick expected to depart in the coming days barring an unexpected development, United could soon need to make a decisive move.

Conte boasts an impressive managerial CV, having won six domestic league titles during his career, including the Premier League with Chelsea and Serie A with both Juventus and Inter Milan.

His reputation for demanding intensity, discipline and high standards could appeal to a club looking for a significant change in direction.

There is an argument that Conte's forceful personality is exactly what United need after another period of instability.

He has a proven ability to transform teams quickly, while his structured tactical approach and preference for physically demanding football could help address some of the weaknesses in United's current side.

Harry Kane, who worked under Conte at Tottenham, previously described the Italian as a "fantastic coach", while his success at Chelsea and across Serie A demonstrates his ability to deliver under pressure.

However, Conte is unlikely to accept the job without significant backing, and that is where United's biggest problem remains.

Whoever replaces Carrick will inherit a lop-sided squad with major holes to fill, so January investment will be essential if the club wants an immediate improvement, rather than simply relying on a change of manager to transform its fortunes.

Conte could certainly shake things up at Old Trafford, but United must be prepared to give him the tools to do so.

#1877. When will Mauricio Pochettino start work at Manchester United? Delay explained after ‘formal contact’

Manchester United have reached a verbal agreement with Mauricio Pochettino, though he will not start work straight away.

Pochettino emerged as the leading candidate to replace Michael Carrick as manager after Sunday’s 4-4 draw against Aston Villa left the former midfielder on the brink, with Man United sitting in the Premier League relegation zone heading into the international break.

The latest reporting is that while Carrick is due to take Man Utd training on Thursday, as he did on both Tuesday and Wednesday, as per the Athletic, the expectation is he will be relieved of his duties at Old Trafford imminently.

Man United CEO Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox are due to return from meetings in Monaco with minority co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe and will then inform Carrick of the decision to dismiss him face-to-face.

In the meantime, United are said to have stepped up their pursuit of Pochettino.

It has been widely reported that United have made formal contact with U.S. Soccer, as they look to appoint the United States Men’s National Team (USMNT) boss as their next head coach.

This development comes following reports overnight that Pochettino’s representatives spent Tuesday discussing personal terms with club officials.

As the Argentine signed an extension with U.S. Soccer as recently as August to continue in his role as national team manager, United are required to activate the $10million (£7.4million), release clause in the 54-year-old’s contract.

However, while United are now looking to finalise an agreement with both Pochettino and U.S. Soccer to make him Carrick’s successor, there is a further complication.

Pochettino is currently with the USMNT ahead of the CONCACAF Nations League two-legged quarter-final against Haiti over the next week, and the expectation is that he is likely to remain in charge of those matches before reporting to Carrington.

Harry Kane believes Manchester United will gain a ‘fantastic manager’ in Mauricio Pochettino if Michael Carrick is sacked.

#1875. Aston Villa transfer news: Unai Emery plotting huge January double swoop as 'dream' target named

By Lewis Blain | 11 Nov 2026 07:34

Aston Villa are preparing for a huge January transfer window, with manager Unai Emery keen to strengthen two key areas of his squad.

The Midlands outfit are prioritising additions in both central midfield and goal, with Gabriel Sara and Santiago Beltran among the names under consideration.

However, Emery also remains interested in a more ambitious attacking addition, with Atletico Madrid maestro Alex Baena continuing to feature on Villa's radar.

According to TEAMtalk, Villa's most concrete interest concerns Galatasaray midfielder Sara, who has been on their shortlist since the summer as a potential successor to Youri Tielemans.

The Turkish club are reportedly open to offers starting at around £33m, although sources suggest a fee closer to £25m could be enough to secure the Brazilian.

Sara's previous experience in English football with Norwich City, combined with his impressive performances in Turkey, makes him an attractive option for Emery.

Premier League rivals Newcastle United, Everton and Brighton & Hove Albion are also monitoring his situation.

Villa are also considering a move for River Plate goalkeeper Beltran, with the 22-year-old having been recommended by the club's scouting department.

The Argentine is viewed as a potential squad addition behind first-choice Zion Suzuki, although the South American giants are attempting to extend his contract and include a significant release clause.

While Sara and Beltran appear to be more realistic January targets, Baena remains an exciting - and 'dream' - possibility for Emery.

The Atletico midfielder previously worked under the Villa boss at Villarreal, and his quality as a World Cup-winning Spain international would represent a major addition in the final third.

However, attracting Baena will be considerably more difficult than pursuing their other targets.

The LaLiga side are reluctant to sell midway through the season, while any deal is expected to cost well over £60m. Arsenal, Bayern Munich and several other major European clubs are also interested, making competition rather fierce.

A January move therefore appears unlikely, with the summer representing a more realistic opportunity, but even then, it could be difficult for Villa to pull off.

Baena would undoubtedly be an ambitious signing for the Villans, but Emery may have to settle for addressing his immediate squad needs before attempting to land his main man.

#1874. Furious Tottenham set to complain to authorities after Jayden Bogle escapes red card in Leeds' 1-0 win at Elland Road

Published: 13:54 EST, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 14:17 EST, 7 November 2026

Tottenham are to issue a formal complaint over the decision not to show a red card to Leeds defender Jayden Bogle after his challenge on Mathys Tel at Elland Road.

Video replays showed Bogle catch the Spurs forward on the back of his left ankle in the first half of Saturday’s lunchtime kick off but despite a lengthy review by the VAR, referee Jon Brooks was not sent to the pitchside monitor.

Tel came back on but was replaced by Dominic Solanke after 43 minutes and Leeds went on to win the game 1-0 through a Noel Okafor goal.

Spurs, who will lodge their protest with Pro Ref, may cite the red card shown to Crystal Palace striker Jean-Philippe Mateta in the previous Saturday’s clash at the Tottenham Stadium for his foul on Micky van de Ven.

On that occasion, referee Michael Oliver originally gave a yellow card but it was upgraded after a video assistant referee review.

Former Premier League assistant referee Darren Cann told BBC that the Leeds defender was ‘fortunate’ not to be dismissed.

Tel came back on but was replaced by Dominic Solanke after 43 minutes and Leeds went on to win the game 1-0

Crystal Palace striker Jean-Philippe Mateta was sent off for this foul on Micky van de Ven in the previous Saturday’s clash

‘Bogle's challenge meets the criteria for serious foul play as he endangers the safety of an opponent,’ Cann said. ‘He can consider himself lucky to still be on the pitch.’

Tottenham manager Roberto De Zerbi was more critical of his own players afterwards, but did say of the decision: 'I have big confidence in the referee. Nothing changes if he goes to the monitor.

'If they didn't take the right decision I don't know. We have to keep the eyes on the performance where can improve.'

The decision will be reviewed by the Key Match Incidents Panel in the coming days. Mateta is serving a three-match suspension after the Football Association rejected Palace's appeal against his red card he received in their 2–0 defeat to Tottenham.

#1872. Mauricio Pochettino to Manchester United latest: £7.4m clause, verbal agreement and transfer targets

Manchester United headed into the final international break of the year with uncertainty over the managerial position, though the next few days are set to prove crucial.

Michael Carrick was left on the brink following Man Utd’s 4-4 draw at home to Aston Villa at the weekend, a result that leaves the side in the Premier League relegation zone after one win from the opening 10 matches.

In a surprising turn of events, Mauricio Pochettino has emerged as the leading contender to replace Carrick at Old Trafford, and it would appear things is gathering pace for some major announcements in the coming hours and days.

Below is what we know about the Man Utd managerial situation.

According to The Athletic, Pochettino’s representatives spent Tuesday discussing personal terms with Manchester United officials, with no major obstacles expected and a final agreement expected.

It has since been reported that United have reached a verbal agreement in principle with Pochettino to take over as head coach, though the Argentine is likely to remain in charge of USA’s CONCACAF Nations League two-legged quarter-final against Haiti.

The second of those ties is in the early hours on Wednesday, November 18 (UK time) which would not give Pochettino too much time with the Man United squad ahead of the Premier League showdown against Liverpool.

For Man Utd to appoint Pochettino, it will not be a cheap deal. This is because the Argentine signed a new contract with US Soccer in August to continue in his role as USMNT manager.

According to The Athletic, there is a buyout clause in Pochettino’s contract worth $10million (£7.44million) which Man Utd can trigger to bring back him to England.

However, the buyout clause does not cover Pochettino’s coaching staff, many of who - such as assistant Jesus Perez - has been with him most the majority of his career.

According to the Athletic, United have now made formal contact with U.S. Soccer, as they look to appoint the United States Men’s National Team (USMNT) boss as their next head coach.

Michael Carrick took training on Tuesday and Wednesday and, as of writing, officially remains Man United boss.

Jamie Redknapp says Andrey Santos is ‘not a Manchester United player’ and claims whoever was responsible for his signing ‘deserves the sack’.

Desperate for midfield reinforcements over the summer, United spent £50m to sign Brazil international Santos from Premier League rivals Chelsea.

Manchester United made midfield targets their priority after Casemiro left Old Trafford and Manuel Ugarte suffered a serious injury at the World Cup.

Carlos Baleba and Youri Tielemans joined Michael Carrick’s squad on top of Santos but all three midfielders have made inauspicious starts to their United careers.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Redknapp doubts the 22-year-old Brazilian is at the level required to play for United and says bringing him to the club was a ‘sackable offence’ by those in charge at Old Trafford.

‘Can I throw one player at you? And this is no disrespect to the boy, because he’s not a bad player, but whoever brought in Andrey Santos, that for me is a sackable offence,’ Redknapp said on The Overlap Daily, sponsored by Sky Vegas.

‘He is not a Manchester United player. He’s a decent player, he’s okay. But they brought [Youri] Tielemans in just after it.

#1870. Arsenal transfer news: Mikel Arteta stance on Piero Hincapie exit now emerges amid Barcelona links

By Lewis Blain | 11 Nov 2026 07:55

Barcelona have expressed an interest in signing Arsenal defender Piero Hincapie ahead of the January transfer window.

However, Gunners boss Mikel Arteta is understood to have no intention of allowing the Ecuador international to leave midway through the season.

Despite limited Premier League opportunities so far in 2026-27, the 24-year-old remains an important part of Arsenal's plans.

According to recent reports, Arsenal have no intention of selling Hincapie during the January transfer window, despite growing interest from the LaLiga giants.

Arteta is keen to maintain two high-quality options in every position as the Gunners compete on multiple fronts, and the versatile defender is viewed as an important part of that strategy.

Hincapie has found opportunities difficult to come by this season, having played just 67 minutes in the Premier League and yet to make a start in the competition.

The former Bayer Leverkusen defender is currently competing with Riccardo Calafiori for the left-back position, but his ability to operate at centre-back also makes him a valuable option.

However, it is also believed that Arsenal would only consider selling him next summer if they could secure an immediate replacement.

The 6-foot defender impressed during his first season at the Emirates, and the expectation is that he will receive more opportunities as the campaign progresses.

Allowing Hincapie to leave in January would be a questionable decision, particularly given the number of competitions Arsenal are attempting to navigate.

His versatility is a major asset for Arteta, who can call upon him at either left-back or centre-back without having to significantly alter his defensive structure.

That flexibility could prove especially valuable if Calafiori suffers further fitness problems, while Hincapie's ability to slot into the heart of defence provides another alternative when rotation is required.

Having two reliable options in each defensive position is essential across a demanding campaign, especially with the Gunners pursuing success in both the Premier League and Champions League.

Hincapie may not currently be a guaranteed starter, but that does not mean he lacks an important role. His opportunities should increase as the fixture schedule becomes more demanding heading into a hectic festive period.

Barcelona's interest is understandable, but Arteta would be foolish to weaken his defensive depth midway through the season unless an exceptional replacement opportunity presented itself.

Pietro Terracciano, Matteo Gabbia, Fikayo Tomori, Alexis Saelemaekers, Ruben Loftus-Cheek, Samuel Chukwueze and Strahinja Pavlovic were all out for the match at the Stadio Luigi Ferraris, with the Serbian centre-back being the latest to enter the treatment room.

“This is essentially a message to the owners, who have already promised to intervene in the January transfer window to fill the gaps. The point is precisely this: until then, the Portuguese coach must continue with his current strength.

#1868. Arsenal injury update: Ezri Konsa, William Saliba, Bukayo Saka latest return dates

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal headed into the international break with a fresh injury concern over Declan Rice, after the midfielder was substituted in the win over Hull.

Those fears have since been allayed with Rice fit enough to join up with the England squad and he is expected to be in action against Croatia on Thursday night.

However, Ezri Konsa will play no part at Wembley Stadium, and there is some concerning news regarding the central defender - who has a fit-again William Saiba breathing down his neck for a starting place.

With that in mind, here is the latest Arsenal injury news and return dates…

Konsa has been managing his fitness after taking a hit to his knee during Arsenal’s 2-1 win away to Slavia Prague.

The defender was able to complete the full 90 minutes at home to Hull three days later, but Thomas Tuchel has confirmed that he will miss England’s Nations League clash at home to Croatia through injury.

“It’s my understanding at the moment that they will be both available but we will not take the risk. For tomorrow, both out for tomorrow,” Tuchel said in his pre-match press conference.

“You saw it, they were not in training. They follow their own programme, and the understanding and the hope and the belief, I would say, is that they’re both in individual training on Friday, team training on Saturday and match ready on Sunday.”

Should Konsa feature for England against Spain on Sunday, then he should be OK for Arsenal’s trip to St James’ Park to face Newcastle in their first game after the international break.

Potential return date: Saturday November 21, vs Newcastle (A)

It is just a matter of time before William Saliba is able to challenge Konsa and Gabriel for a place in the Arsenal defence after a delayed start to the season due to a long-term back injury that he exacerbated while on duty for France at the World Cup.

Saliba was able to avoid surgery, resumed full training before the Slavia Prague game and then travelled with the squad to the Czech Republic.

While Saliba was an unused substitute in Prague and was then left out completely against Hull, he was in action for the U21s the following day, playing 45 minutes of a 5-2 win over Aston Villa.

After being replaced at half-time, Arsenal’s U21s head coach David Horseman confirmed that was always the intention.

Alexander-Arnold completed a dream move to Madrid last year, ending a 21-year spell at boyhood club Liverpool in which he won two Premier League titles and the Champions League.

The England international featured in a little over half of Real Madrid’s league games last season as the Spanish giants endured a rare trophyless campaign.

Competition at right-back only increased over the summer with the arrival of Denzel Dumfries from Inter Milan and Jose Mourinho is currently playing midfielder Federico Valverde in that position.

As a result Alexander-Arnold appears to be third choice and has only earned four starts this season, with his lack of game-time raising speculation over his future at the Bernabeu.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

A return to Liverpool has been raised as a potential possibility given his former club’s issues at right-back, but Glen Johnson has urged Chelsea to bring the 28-year-old to Stamford Bridge.

Chelsea’s first-choice right-back, club captain Reece James, is expected to be out of action until at least mid-January after undergoing knee surgery last month.

‘Trent Alexander-Arnold will definitely be frustrated playing such a small role at Real Madrid this season,’ ex-Liverpool and Chelsea defender Johnson told SeatPick.

‘Before he went to Madrid, he would have planned on nailing down his spot at right back there, and then they brought in a new right back the summer after he arrived, which will have only frustrated him further.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘Trent is a top-class player, and no top-class player wants to sit on the bench, he wants to be playing regular football.

‘I think he should be a target for Chelsea in January. I think they could get him on loan, and it would be perfect for both parties. Chelsea needs a right back at the moment, and Trent needs minutes under his belt.

‘We’ve seen how effective he can be in the Premier League, and if Xabi Alonso could get him back to his best, it would be a great deal to solve a problem for Chelsea and to get his career back on track.’

Liverpool legend Steven Gerrard recently said he would welcome Alexander-Arnold back to Anfield despite the fact his exit upset many fans.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

‘The decision he made and all the stuff around it, do I think it would be the right thing for Liverpool’s group now and the supporters? I’m going to sit on the fence and say I’m unsure,’ Gerrard told The Overlap Daily.

‘Ability-wise, talent-wise, what he’d done for Liverpool in terms of the success, I would say yes, but the ending and that still being a little bit raw…

‘I would, yes, myself personally. So I won’t sit on the fence because that’s poor from me. I would, yes.

‘Do I think it’s the right thing for this group now, this manager now and where Liverpool are at right now? I’m unsure. Does he make the Liverpool team and squad better? He does, 100 per cent.

‘It’s tough, it’s tough. I would, yes, and ability-wise, yes, I’m just not sure it’s right for the group, right now.’

Liverpool are fourth in the Premier League heading into the November international break, one place and two points above Chelsea.

Alexander-Arnold’s current club Real Madrid are second in La Liga, having recently closed the gap on leaders Barcelona to just three points with an El Clasico win at the Nou Camp.

Alan Smith believes that Arsenal should consider offering Martin Zubimendi to Atletico Madrid as part of a swap deal to sign Julian Alvarez.

Zubimendi’s future at Arsenal has come into question in recent weeks, with the Spaniard still yet to start a Premier League match this season.

The central midfielder made an immediate impact after signing from Real Sociedad for £60million 18 months ago, starting 34 matches as Mikel Arteta’s side ended their 22-year wait for another league title.

Fatigue, however, eventually caught up with Zubimendi at the end of last season and his place was effectively taken by teenager Myles Lewis-Skelly, who started in his place in the Champions League final.

Lewis-Skelly’s continued form, as well as the high-profile summer arrival of Bruno Guimaraes, has seen Zubimendi slide down the pecking order in north London and sparked speculation that a January move could be on the cards for the World Cup winner.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Atletico Madrid are reportedly keen to bring Zubimendi back to La Liga, and Smith believes the Gunners can use that interest to finally strike a deal for Alvarez, who they were heavily interested in over the summer.

‘Obviously he played a big part last season, but having been an ever-present, he might be getting a bit restless not to be getting starts, just to be coming off the bench for a few minutes, Smith told Best Betting Sites.

‘So that might be something that can be part of a bargaining chip for Arsenal.

‘If you could do a part swap, then obviously you’re not shelling out over 100 million pounds on Alvarez, because I’m sure Atletico would want something well in excess of that. So that might be a way forward.

#1864. Man United next manager: Business as usual for Michael Carrick, but Mauricio Pochettino arrival is 'imminent'

By Matt Law | 11 Nov 2026 09:00, Last updated: 11 Nov 2026 09:03

Manchester United are reportedly finalising a deal to appoint Mauricio Pochettino as their next head coach, with Michael Carrick expected to be sacked.

A disastrous start to the 2026-27 campaign has left Man United down in 18th spot in the Premier League table, winning just one of their 10 league matches this season.

Man United twice fought back from two goals behind against Aston Villa on Sunday to draw 4-4, but the result is seemingly not enough for Carrick to keep his job.

According to The Athletic, Man United are currently finalising a deal to bring Pochettino to Old Trafford, should Carrick be relived of his duties.

The report claims that the Red Devils spent Tuesday discussing personal terms with Pochettino, who is currently in charge of the United States national team.

However, no contact has been made with US Soccer at this stage of proceedings.

It is understood that Man United would need to pay a fee in the region of £7.4m in order to release Pochettino from his contract with the USA.

Further compensation would be required to bring in Pochettino's staff members, which is also expected to be paid, such is Man United's desire to appoint the Argentine.

Pochettino has a contract with the United States until the end of the 2030 World Cup, but his time with the national team is seemingly about to end.

The 54-year-old has previously managed Southampton, Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea in the Premier League, but he has always had a desire to manage the Red Devils.

Man United's director of football Jason Wilcox and CEO Omar Berrada are set to meet with the club's co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe in Monaco on Wednesday.

It is understood that Wilcox and Berrada will recommend to Ratcliffe to remove Carrick from his position at Old Trafford.

Carrick took Man United training on Tuesday and is again at Carrington on Wednesday morning to oversee a session which will largely feature academy players.

Pochettino's first match in charge of Man United is set to be the clash with Liverpool at Anfield after the November international break.

Pochettino is set to take charge at Old Trafford and replace Michael Carrick, who will be sacked following a dismal start to the season.

But United chose Pochettino as their first-choice pick this week and are currently finalising a deal to bring the Argentine back to the Premier League.

Pochettino, who will step down from his role as head coach of the USA to take over at Manchester United, has already worked at fellow English clubs Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea, as well as Spanish side Espanyol and French giants PSG.

One of the biggest problems for United this season has been a fragile defence and ex-Premier League striker Charlie Austin insists Pochettino ‘needs a whole new back-four’.

Austin believes Pochettino could look to sign someone like Rudiger, the Real Madrid and Germany centre-back who previously spent five years in England with Chelsea.

#1860. Serbia vs Germany - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matt Law | 11 Nov 2026 10:10, Last updated: 11 Nov 2026 10:13

Germany are under pressure to pick up all three points heading into their penultimate 2026-27 UEFA Nations League group fixture against Serbia on Friday night.

Jurgen Klopp's side are third in Group A2, three points behind second-placed Greece, while Serbia are at the bottom on zero points and cannot qualify for the quarter-finals.

There is no getting away from the fact that it has been a tough UEFA Nations League campaign for Serbia, with the national side losing all four of their fixtures in Group A2.

The Eagles opened up with a 2-1 home loss to Greece before going down 2-1 against Netherlands in their second match in the section; a 2-0 loss to Germany followed in their third fixture.

Veljko Paunovic's side were then beaten 2-1 by Netherlands in their last match, and they can no longer finish in the top two in Group A2, although it is still possible to claim third ahead of Germany, with a win required in this match to stand any chance of that occurring.

Serbia have lost each of their last six matches in all competitions, while they have only won once since the end of 2025, so it has been a tough period.

The national side have faced Germany on four previous occasions, boasting a record of one win, one draw and two defeats, with their victory coming in the group stage of the 2010 World Cup.

Germany will know the importance of picking up all three points in this match if they are to stand a chance of securing a top-two spot and advancing to the quarter-finals.

Klopp's side have a record of one win, two draws and one defeat from four games in the section, and they are three points off both second-placed Greece and leaders Netherlands with two matches left.

The National Eleven started their Group A2 campaign with a 1-1 draw against Netherlands before suffering a shock 1-0 home loss to Greece at the end of September.

Germany managed to post an important 2-0 win over Serbia at the start of October, but they were then held to a goalless draw by Greece, so DFB-Team are playing catch-up ahead of their final two fixtures against Serbia and Netherlands.

Anything less than four points from their final two matches would make qualification highly unlikely, but successive wins would take them onto 11 points and could potentially be enough to advance to the final eight of the Nations League.

Serbia will be without the services of two players through suspension, with Sasa Lukic and Nemanja Maksimovic ruled out of the contest with Germany.

Aleksandar Mitrovic is in line to win his 107th cap for his country, and the 32-year-old could be joined in the final third of the field by Mihajlo Cvetkovic, who has one goal in five matches for Serbia.

There is also set to be a spot in the middle of the midfield for Sergej Milinkovic-Savic.

Germany, meanwhile, have three players one booking away from a suspension, with Philipp Treu, Malick Thiaw and Yann Bisseck all in danger of missing the team's final fixture in the group stage of the 2026-27 Nations League.

Kai Havertz has scored 25 times for Germany and is once again expected to feature through the middle, while Florian Wirtz could also be in line for a starting role on Friday.

Said El Mala and Lennart Karl could be involved from the first whistle, while Marc-Andre ter Stegen has been confirmed as Germany's number one goalkeeper.

V Milinkovic-Savic; Nedeljkovic, Gudelj, Babic, Erakovic, Sukacev; Samardzic, S Milinkovic-Savic, Zivkovic; Cvetkovic, Mitrovic

Ter Stegen; Treu, Tah, Schlotterbeck, Brown; Nmecha, Kimmich; El Mala, Wirtz, Karl; Havertz

Germany have been far from convincing in this Nations League tournament, but Serbia have also struggled, and we are backing Klopp's side to secure a valuable three points on Friday.

City’s rumoured pursuit of Gusto stretches back for some time, with Enzo Maresca understood to have been keen on a reunion with the full-back when he took over the reins at the Etihad in the summer.

Gusto has three-and-a-half years remaining on his current contract with Chelsea.

There are, of course, complications for both United and City when it comes to potential transfer dealings this January, with the former reportedly on the verge of a managerial change and the latter still yet to learn their punishment for Premier League rule breaches.

Gusto filled in as a makeshift midfielder during Moises Caicedo’s absence from the team through injury and there were some suggestions the Frenchman could continue in the role under Alonso.

But speaking exclusively to Metro at the time, ex-Chelsea midfielder Gus Poyet insisted Gusto should look to earn Alonso’s trust by becoming the best possible right-back.

‘I do remember one of the most impressive decisions by a coach – Pep Guardiola at Bayern Munich, playing Lahm as a central midfielder,’ Poyet explained.

‘It was big news at the time, because he had the quality. Chelsea have been doing this with Reece James, because they understand it’s a possibility. Now Gusto as well.

‘But any right-back becoming a good central midfielder? No chance. Because full-backs naturally get used to playing with the line next to them, either on their right side or their left. Nobody’s coming at them from that side, because you’ve got the line.

‘Now, when you play in the middle, players come at you from everywhere, and not every player is the same. So yes, for one game [they can play there]. Yes, for twenty minutes. Not constantly. And now we see Chelsea playing a right-back as a central midfielder every game.

‘This is Chelsea — we’re not talking about a fourth-division club with no possibility of bringing in a player. So yes, it’s a little bit strange. And I don’t think it’s ideal.’
