#1858. How Harry Kane bucked every trend to become England's superstar

England’s greatest goalscorer makes yet more history tonight

Jose Mourinho once sat with Harry Kane in the manager’s office at Tottenham’s training ground and explained the difference between the two men.

Kane was a much younger 26-year-old then, the reigning World Cup Golden Boot winner but not considered truly world class outside of England. A prolific striker for club and country, nothing more.

“I have no doubt: you are a winner,” said Mourinho, on his second day in the Spurs job. He felt, though, that “the movie stars of football belong to other places”, that Kane was no superstar. In one of those rare moments when Mourinho brought the topic of conversation back to himself, he insisted that, by contrast, “my dimension is universal”.

“We have to build your status in that direction,” Mourinho said.

In the intervening six years, Kane has done so by himself, through dogged determination, constant refining of his craft, and the relentlessness that staying at the top of the sport for so long necessitates, not needing the help of Mourinho or anyone else.

Against Croatia tonight, Kane dons England colours for a record 126th time, 98 as captain, as he overtakes Peter Shilton’s tally. He will do so 17 days after beating Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal to win the Ballon d’Or aged 33 years young, crowned the best footballer in the world.

He scored 73 goals for club and country last season, goalscoring of such mechanical, clockwork regularity it saw him surpass Cristiano Ronaldo’s best-ever campaign. Kane’s tally marked the second-greatest season of goalscoring in football’s modern history, trailing only the superhuman tally of 82 goals in 69 games posted by Lionel Messi in 2011-12. He had mentioned wanting to emulate Messi and Ronaldo in that 2019 heart-to-heart with Mourinho.

Yet stats have not always been kind to Kane. No matter the endless individual honours, the reminders of an empty trophy cabinet stalked him for years until his Bundesliga title win with Bayern last year. He is still awaiting a first Champions League title and a major trophy with England after two European Championship finals, two World Cup semi-finals and a quarter-final despite two major tournament Golden Boots.

The latter of those two Golden Boots, which he shared with five other players, arrived at Euro 2024, where he looked out of sorts while nursing a back injury and had to field straight-faced suggestions Gareth Southgate should drop him for Ollie Watkins. He stuck to the task and outscored everyone at the tournament anyway. He has 91 goals for England now, and this summer overtook Pelé for World Cup goals, scoring his 14 at a quicker rate of return than Messi and Ronaldo scored theirs.

Kane’s is a learnt talent ... four EFL loan spells toughened up one of football’s great late bloomers

And that has been Kane’s enduring quality: he delivers reliable results, England’s royal male. Kane was 33 years and 90 days old when he lifted the Ballon d’Or, fitting for a player who has only improved with age, whose nous and understanding of the game have combined with that unshakable self-belief to take him to heights not even he had envisioned.

He last week signed a new contract at Bayern Munich believed to make him Europe’s highest-paid player by base salary.

Kane is at his peak. As a player, first you are physically good, then you get older and have to get smarter because you can’t physically keep doing what your more efficient brain wants you to. Kane is in the cross-section — still a physical specimen but with that mature footballing IQ to boot. It is an irresistible sight to behold.

Comfortably the best player during his Tottenham years, where he became the club’s record goalscorer, the move to Bayern in 2023 has elevated him and made him better appreciated around the world.

Bayern’s honorary president, Uli Hoeness, declared him the greatest signing the club have ever made on the eve of May’s German Cup final. Kane then scored a hat-trick in a 3-0 win as they won the trophy for the first time in six years.

Bayern have come to appreciate the player Tottenham and England fans always knew they had — the striker whose tall frame and lack of searing pace disguise a Swiss Army Knife reality. For almost a decade, discussion has raged over whether Kane should drop deep as he does or should stay in the box. His sublime raking passes and deftly-weighted through-balls at a moment’s notice were enough to convince Mourinho, Southgate, Vincent Kompany and now Thomas Tuchel that Kane is best when he does as he pleases.

The romance of Kane’s story is that he is one of football’s sight-readers rather than playing his music by ear. His is a learnt talent, honed by repetition. Four EFL loan spells toughened up one of football’s great late bloomers.

That robotic repetition in training has made him a penalty specialist and a sumptuous ball-striker with an instinctive shooting ability, the ball immediately out of his feet and then driven, often low, precisely into the corner as though placed there by hand.

A 21-year-old Kane impressed in pre-season for Tottenham in 2014, yet Pochettino sat him down and informed him his body fat test result of 18 per cent was the highest in the team. Pochettino urged him to work harder: “You can be the best striker in the world.” Kane’s unwavering belief in that statement is, more than anything, what has propelled him there.

Anthony Gordon this summer gave the definitive assessment of what it is like to work with Walthamstow’s finest.

It is no accident. Every drill, he does it with seriousness. He never ever messes about

“Anyone at this level can put the ball in the top corner,” Gordon said. “It’s his consistency every single day in training and every game. He’s having a season that has only ever been beaten by the greatest footballer of all time; that speaks to the level he is playing at. You want to pick up as many habits and watch everything he does, to see why he is at that level.

“It is no accident. Every drill, he does it with seriousness. He never ever messes about.”

The complete player, he has spent the last 12 years representing Tottenham, Bayern and England and been the central cog in all three machines, never knowing anything other than being the man to whom others turn.

Some of his rivals for the Ballon d’Or had launched cringey PR campaigns when voting went live. In an answer to The Standard about this, he admitted in the lead up: “It’s just not my personality to talk about myself in that light.”

His body of work spoke for itself in the end. His acceptance speech featured motivation young children heading to Wembley on Thursday evening could do with hearing. “Anything is possible with hard work when no one else is watching.” Everyone is watching him now.

Ahead of another record-breaking night for England’s captain and leader by example, it is worth asking: has Kane proven Mourinho wrong? A movie star? Even now, not really his style. But by staying in his lane and grafting in silence, Kane has joined them — working his way up to the leading role, in his own, very English, way.

#1857. RECAP: Nottingham Forest 3-1 Man City - Premier League: Enzo Maresca's men suffer third defeat in a row, as Liam Delap stars to lift his side out of drop zone - at Man United's expense

RDaily Mail Sport's live coverage of Nottingham Forest vs Man City.

Oliver Glasner channelled his inner Jose Mourinho when Delap scored Forest's third goal, sprinting down the touchline to celebrate with his players.

In such a precarious job, this victory will mean a lot to him. There's never any guarantee of owner Evangelos Marinakis' patience.

For the first time since 2024, Manchester City have lost three consecutive games in the top fliight.

They're also just the second team in top-flight history to win their first seven games then lose the next three. The previous side to do that were Sheffield Wednesday in 1904-05.

I suspect they'll beat Fulham after the international break, but you never know!

Manchester United end a day in the bottom three of the to -flight after having played at least nine games for the first time since November 1986.

Ouch. Thanks to Opta for the stat. They'll be looking to make amends against Aston Villa tomorrow but I don't back them.

Donnarumma had another poor game today, looking flappy. I'm not sure there was much he could have done about the goals, which were all worthy strikes, but conceding three goals won't help a man who has come under increasing scrutiny in recent weeks.

Here's why Maresca stood by him. Do you think it's time for a change?

Why Maresca is sticking with Donnarumma despite Leipzig horror show

JACK GAUGHAN: These are tough times for Donnarumma, a calamitous night in the Champions League adding to the feeling that the past few weeks have not reflected kindly on him.

Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol looked lost today. Enzo Maresca hooked the at half-time after each was at fault for one of the goals. Gvardiol was asleep, giving away the ball for the first, and Guehi just retreated as Delap ran towards goal for the second.

Worrying. Guehi has looked shorn of confidence in recent weeks and this isn't the first time he's been withdrawn at the break.

Today we saw the version of Delap which we know he can be. An absolute bulldozer.

His main flaw is that he typically lacks the finishing. To demonstrate: coming into today, he had scored just two Premier League goals since the start of LAST season. Not a good look.

Well, his finishing was explosive here, as was his running and strength. He's scary when he plays like that.

Manchester United have never been in the relegation zone at this stage of a Premier League season before. Truly abysmal for them.

As for Forest, they can smile after being rewarded for their good performance. They're far from out of the woods, but they did two key things today: score at home, and get Liam Delap's confidence up. Both are critical.

Maresca straight down the tunnel and it didn’t seem as if there was a handshake between him and Oliver Glasner. Dismal night for City but the performance is in keeping with how they are playing. So susceptible on the break and when you’re making this many individual mistakes then the opponents know that they can just wait for them.

Liam Delap has been speaking to Sky Sports.

'It's been coming. We've been performing like that every week but not putting it in the net,' he said.

'We did everything right, got the three points, and are happy going into the international break.

'I just wanted to run and shoot and luckily go there and it went in the net (for first goal).

'Thankfully I put it in the net (for the second).

'We'll have to see it back (Glasner's run down the touchline). Never (seen him run like that).

'We've been deserving this for a long time. Hopefully we can build on it.'

Man City have now lost three times on the spin in the Premier League. Whatever faux title charge they were mounting is collapsing fast at this rate.

The full time whistle blows an Oliver Glasner fist pumps. A HUGE win for Nottingham Forest, one which propels them out of the relegation zone, and plunges Manchester United into it.

#1856. Man Utd sack Michael Carrick and provide update on Mauricio Pochettino arrival

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Manchester United have sacked Michael Carrick with Mauricio Pochettino set to be appointed their new head coach.

Carrick led training at Carrington this week despite it becoming clear a change was imminent as early as Monday evening.

He arrived at United’s training base at Carrington just before 8am on Thursday morning, leaving less than two-and-a-half hours later having been relieved of his duties.

Behind the scenes, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox have sought approval from minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe to part ways with Carrick, with a deal for Pochettino, currently serving as the USA men’s head coach, in place.

Carrick has been on the brink at various stages this season with United sat in the relegation zone in 18th place after 10 games, winning just once against newly promoted Ipswich Town.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

United opted against making a change during the international break in September and October when Julian Nagelsmann and Eddie Howe were the leading contenders for the job.

Carrick gave himself a lifeline as United came from behind to beat Roma in the Champions League at the start of the month. United also fought back twice from 2-1 down in the same game against Aston Villa on Sunday to rescue a 4-4 draw but the decision was made the following day to part ways with the former midfielder.

His staff are also expected to leave, including former defender Jonny Evans who was pictured leaving Carrington with his belongings on Wednesday.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Carrick’s departure marks the third season in a row United have sacked a manager midway through the campaign.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Pochettino’s first game in charge is expected to be the visit to Liverpool on Sunday 22 November.

Carrick, who had a brief spell as interim boss in 2021, took the reins again in January following Ruben Amorim’s dismissal, securing hugely impressive wins over Manchester City and Arsenal in his opening two games.

They won 12 of their 17 games during the second-half of the 2025-26 season, securing third place and Champions League qualification with a game to spare. United picked up more points than champions Arsenal managed in the period from Carrick’s game in charge until the end of the campaign.

United clearly benefited from the lighter schedule in that run with just the Premier League to focus on. With European football back on the menu this season, reinforcements were needed.

United signed three new midfielders in the summer in Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba but missed out on their top targets Elliot Anderson and Mateus Fernandes who joined Manchester City and Tottenham respectively.

The club also failed to sign another left-back and a striker – positions they were in desperate need of cover for. United are paying the price now with Luke Shaw and Benjamin Sesko injured.

Before the comeback victory over Roma, United’s only wins this season came at home to Ipswich and against Azerbaijan outfit Sabah. Following a particularly harrowing defeat to Como in the Champions League, club captain Bruno Fernandes publicly challenged the manager’s tactics with the skipper dropped for the subsequent game against Chelsea.

Following the 3-0 defeat at home to Bournemouth, Carrick was applauded off the pitch by supporters who instead turned their ire towards the players in a clear picture of where the frustration lies.

#1854. Luxembourg vs Estonia - prediction, team news, lineups

By Darren Plant | 11 Nov 2026 10:10

Estonia square off against Luxembourg on Friday evening knowing that victory could guarantee them a top-two spot in UEFA Nations League Group C4.

However, despite sitting bottom of the group, Luxembourg can move level on points with their second-placed opponents with a win in Luxembourg City.

Although Iceland were the favourites for this group before it began, it was an evenly-match draw that gave chances to all four nations.

That is how it has panned out, with bottom-placed Luxembourg trailing leaders Iceland by five points with two matches remaining.

Luxembourg began their campaign with a 2-1 victory in Bulgaria, but losing 3-0 at home to Iceland in their following fixture seemingly dented their belief.

Further defeats to Estonia and Bulgaria, without scoring a goal, have extended their losing streak to three games, yet they remain in a position where they could earn a spot in the promotion playoffs.

Jeff Strasser's side remain 21 places above Estonia in the FIFA World Rankings in 101st position, a consequence of having won four of five matches prior to their recent run without success.

However, Estonia are currently on a six-game unbeaten streak, a period where they have conceded just the one goal.

While their solitary success in this group is a 1-0 triumph over Luxembourg in the reverse fixture, Jurgen Henn's team have twice held Iceland to low-scoring draws and also shared the spoils with Bulgaria.

If Estonia beat Luxembourg and Iceland win in Bulgaria on Friday, they will be guaranteed a place in the promotion playoffs with one match to spare.

Each of their last three wins on the international stage have been by 1-0 scorelines.

With Dick Carlson serving a one-match ban for accumulating two yellow cards, Florian Bohnert could move into the middle of the Luxembourg backline.

That would allow captain Laurent Jans to return at right-back after he missed the last two matches due to injury.

Sebastien Thill and Aiman Dardari are alternatives in midfield and the final third if Strasser wants to make further alterations.

There will be at least two changes to the Estonia XI with Marten Kuusk and Robi Saarma not featuring in Henn's squad.

Captain Karol Mets could slot into the back three, while Karel Mustmaa may be introduced into the attack.

Mattias Kait - the only player in the Estonia squad with more than three international goals - is an option to return in central midfield.

Moris; Jans, Bohnert, Selimovic, Veiga; Cruz; Natami, V Thill, Dos Santos, Kadamani; Videira

Igonen; Mets, Paskotsi, Tougjas; Peetson, Palumets, Kristal, Poom, Saliste; Mustmaa, Mannilaan

With Estonia having shown their defensive quality at this level, it will be difficult for Luxembourg to get on the scoresheet. After Estonia beat Luxembourg by the solitary goal in their first meeting in October, we feel that a repeat scoreline could occur here.

‘Because if they have Dorgu at left-back, Mazraoui at right-back and Yoro and Heaven at centre-back, he will have to do one hell of a job coaching to get them up the league.’

Neville added: ‘The back four that he finished with on Sunday was Dalot left-back, Mazraoui right-back, Lenny Yoro and Ayden Heaven. That is probably the worst back four in the Premier League.

‘I don’t know a back four that is worse than that in the Premier League right now if I watch it. That is… I can’t believe Manchester United have ended up with that back four.’

#1849. Mauricio Pochettino stance on Bruno Fernandes revealed before Manchester United move

Mauricio Pochettino looks set to finally get his wish as he closes in on being appointed as the new Manchester United manager.

It is expected that Michael Carrick will be sacked, with United spending the international break in the relegation zone after a dismal start to the season.

Carrick has not yet officially been relieved of his duties but United have held talks with Pochettino and he is said to be keen on the job.

Pochettino signed a contract extension with the United States national team in the summer, meaning United will have to pay a release clause of around £7.5million.

The arrival of Pochettino could be good news for Bruno Fernandes, as he looks to rediscover his best form.

In the summer of 2019, Pochettino was in charge at Tottenham and pushed hard to bring Fernandes, then still a Sporting player, to north London.

Fernandes was desperate to make the move but Sporting held firm. Six months later, he signed for United.

“Obviously I wanted to go to the Premier League,” Fernandes told The Athletic, reflecting on that period.

“The [Tottenham] manager, Mauricio Pochettino, was the one who wanted me there. It was a good offer but Sporting tried their best to keep me.

“The president spoke with me but he spoke with me on the wrong day. It was the day after they decided to refuse the offer from Tottenham and I was really angry.”

Carrick sack news LIVE: Man Utd latest as Pochettino deal agreed

Man Utd injury update: Latest return dates for first Pochettino game

Pochettino to Man Utd latest after verbal agreement to become manager

Winter escapes and activities to end the year in style

Fernandes broke the Premier League assist record last season but he has been well off his best since the start of this campaign.

He has four goals and two assists in the league, but those all came in two matches against Ipswich and Aston Villa.

A fresh start in terms of managers will be good news for Fernandes, who has had a tense relationship with Carrick in recent weeks.

After United’s 4-1 Champions League defeat by Como, Fernandes took aim at the tactics that Carrick and his coaching staff had implemented. The United captain was dropped for the following match.

Club sources indicated that Fernandes then returned to the team after clear-the-air talks with Carrick, but the midfielder dismissed that.

“A lot of lies around many things that have happened between me and the manager,” Fernandes said.

“That we have cleared the air, then after that the manager took the decision to put me on the bench because I’m not performing. That’s fair.

“Everyone thought that was a punishment for the words that I had. And, if it was, it was right. The manager is the one who makes the decisions.”

It is now set to be Pochettino’s job to keep Fernandes happy and get him performing on a consistent basis again.

At Tottenham, Pochettino developed Dele Alli into an elite midfielder. When he then took charge of Chelsea, Cole Palmer played his best football for the Blues with Pochettino in the dugout.

They are both different types of player to Fernandes, but Pochettino’s record of getting attacking midfielders to thrive under his guidance bodes well.

More than seven years after trying to sign Fernandes, Pochettino is set to finally get the chance to show what he can do with him.

#1848. Mauricio Pochettino will ditch four Man Utd stars – the winners and losers under new boss

Mauricio Pochettino is poised to take the reins at Manchester United in the club’s latest attempt to reset the clock.

Having been regarded as a genuine candidate for the job at Old Trafford on three occasions in the past, the Argentine now gets his chance in Manchester where United’s situation is more dire than ever.

With Michael Carrick’s exit confirmed, Pochettino will inherit a squad that has been routinely booed off the pitch by a fanbase thoroughly disenchanted with a lack of effort on it. While there may be hopes of recruitment in the January transfer window, Pochettino will have to work with what he has at his disposal until then.

Metro looks across the United squad to identify whose prospects look brighter than ever with the new manager en route – and those who face the axe.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

With Benjamin Sesko starting just two matches this season before injury struck again, Bryan Mbeumo has spent most of the campaign operating up top. He could remain in that role until Sesko is fit again but both he and Matheus Cunha stand to benefit in their natural positions under the new regime.

Pochettino has favoured inverted wingers to help create overloads in the middle with Cunha in particular tailor made for that role.

Moussa Dembele evolved into one of the Premier League’s most dominant midfielders at Tottenham under Pochettino, carrying on the work started by Martin Jol at Fulham with the Belgian. Kobbie Mainoo lacks Dembele’s outstanding athleticism but his press resistance and running power with the ball will be regarded as key assets for Pochettino.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Mainoo does not have the constant high-energy output Pochettino has traditionally demanded of his midfielders but he has improved his engine over the last two years and his ability to break the lines could also see him play a key role.

Erik ten Hag, Ruben Amorim and Michael Carrick all lauded the qualities of Mason Mount despite injuries ensuring they never saw the best of him. Pochettino could be another to look favourably upon him if he can prove his fitness.

When in negotiations with Chelsea back in 2023, Pochettino was eager for the club to end a contract stand-off with the midfielder and was desperate to keep him and make him a key component of his rebuild west London. His own arrival came too late to revive negotiations however with Mount joining United that summer.

Mount’s work rate has never been in doubt and his abilities to run off the ball or intelligently drop into space could be vital. But with just one start in the Premier League this season, the same old doubts are in place.

In October, former United captain Gary Neville called time on the Mainoo-Youri Tielemans partnership, neither dynamic or athletic enough to last the course in the Premier League. There may only be one winner with the Belgian perhaps most at risk.

Tielemans is adept in keeping possession and progressing play but his lack of drive up the pitch is seemingly at odds with how Pochettino likes to set up his midfield. Pochettino was also said to have turned down the chance to sign the midfielder on at least one occasion after his name was put forward by the Tottenham board.

The same concerns for Tielemans could also apply for another summer recruit in Andrey Santos who looks to be another passive operator based on evidence to date.

The emphasis Pochettino puts on his full-backs has been huge during his time in the Premier League but it is the area of the pitch where United are perhaps at their weakest. Diogo Dalot’s shortcomings on the right continue to be exposed while a long-term replacement for Luke Shaw is well overdue.

Dalot’s prospects are brighter – while his final ball is consistently short of the required standard, his ability to get up and down the pitch will be important. Shaw can no longer offer that kind of service on the left and Pochettino may favour the energy of Patrick Dorgu.

Pochettino helped nurture Shaw at Southampton before his £27million move to Manchester in 2014 but the 31-year-old will now struggle to provide the intensity the role demands.

United’s defence has been an utter mess and with the exception of perhaps Leny Yoro, all should consider their futures uncertain. But at 34, Maguire is perhaps the most at risk.

Pochettino favours a high defensive line, requiring centre-halves with pace to live with it. Maguire will turn 34 in March and has been at the heart of a backline that has conceded 19 goals in 10 Premier League games this season.

Pochettino may favour the younger legs of Yoro and Ayden Heaven while Lisandro Martinez’s ability to build from the back could keep him in the picture for now.

#1847. GdS: Week-long breaks and lighter sessions – Amorim bringing ‘international culture’ to Milanello

Ruben Amorim’s decisions when it comes to training have once again come under the microscope after the win over Genoa.

La Gazzetta dello Sport report that Amorim’s closing message to the players after the victory at the Marassi was music to their ears: ‘See you next Monday’. Until early next week, Milanello will remain closed, leaving the players free to recover from the early season grind.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Who knows if things might have been different had the trip to Genoa had gone differently, but the victory that put Milan back in the Champions League spot is worth the reward of a full seven days off. in the eyes of the coach.

An oddity: Serie A teams usually have a break during the international break, but not this long. It’s also worth noting that Milan’s 13 internationals are currently busy traveling around Europe and the world, while the injured players will also continue to follow their respective recovery programs.

As a reminder, Amorim gave those who were not called up by their national teams eight days off for the last international break. However, if must be remembered that it was an extended three-week one, so there was more runway before games resumed.

The extended break is not the first change introduced by Amorim and his staff. For example, the Tuesday rest granted to the team on the eve of the European trip to Bournemouth. The Rossoneri returned to the pitch on Wednesday, the same day they left for England.

This is an unusual approach compared to the traditional post-match rest schedule or a maximum of three or four days of rest during league breaks. Amorim’s training methods are also new, exemplifying the ‘international culture’ the coach seeks to instil at Milanello.

On the pitch, the sessions are never too hard or tiring. The Portuguese coach himself explained the thinking behind it, emphasising that among the many matches scheduled, the tactics and movements were essentially practiced in-game due to the limited time available between matches.

The concept of over-working players in training amidst a demanding fixture list was thought to be the cause of the many Milan injuries suffered during similar periods. Amorim has sought to rectify it, but then the list of absences for the Genoa game was long, so it all remains a work in progress.

#1846. Alan Shearer hails Arsenal star as the early ‘player of the season’ in the Premier League

Alan Shearer has hailed Arsenal summer signing Ezri Konsa as the early ‘player of the season’ in the Premier League.

Konsa completed a £55m move to Arsenal over the summer after ending his seven-year spell at Aston Villa.

The England defender won the Europa League at Villa Park but has bigger ambitions with reigning Premier League champions and Champions League finalists Arsenal.

Konsa has missed just one game for Arsenal so far this season, helping Mikel Arteta’s side open up a five-point gap at the top of the Premier League and enjoy an impressive start to their European campaign.

The 29-year-old was signed partly due to the absence of William Saliba, who returned from last summer’s World Cup with a serious back injury.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

But Konsa’s form has led several pundits to question whether Saliba, widely regarded as one of the best defenders in the world, will even get straight back into the Arsenal team.

‘I think the player of the season up to now has been Ezri Konsa,’ Premier League record goalscorer and former England striker Shearer told Betfair.

‘I just think when you look at the performances of Arsenal defensively, and look at his performances defensively, we haven’t even really mentioned them missing William Saliba.

‘The only time we’ve mentioned him is in the last two weeks and that’s because everyone is thinking how is he going to get back in because Konsa has been that good.’

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Earlier this week Manchester United legend Rio Ferdinand said Konsa’s brilliant start at Arsenal had created a ‘problem’ for Arteta.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

‘Mikel Arteta has got a problem, he’s got a huge problem now,’ Ferdinand said on his YouTube channel.

‘What is he going to do when William Saliba is fit? Ezri Konsa has come into that back-four and he looks like he’s been there for ten years.

‘He looks like an immovable object in that team. That’s what it feels like because he’s just slid in there and taken that place. He looks dominant, aggressive and accustomed to wearing the Arsenal shirt.

‘He looks like he belongs there. But let’s not forget about Saliba and what he was doing when he was in the team. It’s a problem but it’s a problem that I hope Mikel Arteta will enjoy because he’s got two top centre-backs vying to be in the team.

‘It’s a good position to be in. I think we will see Konsa sometimes playing right-back.’

Arsenal’s nearest challengers going into the November international break is Brighton, who have won seven of their ten league games to climb to second in the Premier League.

‘Brighton could be Arsenal’s main challenge to the title this season,’ Shearer added.

‘I think Liverpool are in transition. Chelsea, same thing. They still have plenty of work to do with those football clubs.

‘Brighton have been incredible. The football that they’re playing, I mean, in Europe too, whether that will hinder them the longer the season goes on I don’t know, but they’re managing really well at the minute.

‘I don’t think they’re going to go away. I think there’ll be around for the majority of the season.’

Arsenal’s first game back following the international break is a potentially tricky trip to St James’ Park to face Newcastle United.

#1844. England Under-21s vs Portugal Under-21s - prediction, team news, lineups

By Darren Plant | 11 Nov 2026 10:40, Last updated: 11 Nov 2026 16:21

England Under-21s and Portugal Under-21s square off in an international friendly at Ashton Gate on Friday night.

These nations have booked their place at the European Under-21 Championship next summer.

While England Under-21s have won the last two European Championships, they are not showing the kind of form which suggests that they can win a third crown in a row.

Even prior to losing 3-1 in Republic of Ireland in their most recent fixture, Lee Carsley had witnessed his team held to a 1-1 draw in Andorra and only record a 4-2 triumph over Kazakhstan on home territory.

Just one clean sheet has been kept in five games, that coming in a goalless draw at home to Slovakia.

Although England did enough to win their qualification group with a game to spare, their defensive record indicates that they will be outsiders when it comes to the next major tournament.

With Chelsea's Josh Acheampong having withdrawn from the squad through injury, there are no defenders in the squad who play regular Premier League football.

Luis Freire's have hardly been perfect themselves, with a 2-1 defeat to Bulgaria having been posted in September.

However, Portugal have incredibly won their other 10 matches across an 11-game period with a clean sheet.

Either side of the Bulgaria setback, 10 goals have been netted in fixtures versus Northern Ireland, Gibraltar and Czech Republic.

As much as Carsley's team need to test themselves against opposition of the level of Portugal, Freire will want to see how his players handle England's attacking flair.

These teams last squared off as recently as March 2025, with England recording a 4-2 victory at The Hawthorns.

Portugal Under-21s form (all competitions):

With the likes of Josh King, Tyler Dibling and Will Lankshear not in the England Under-21s squad, changes will be made in midfield and attack.

Jack Hinshelwood may be drafted into midfield, while Divin Mubama could get the nod as the number nine.

Liverpool midfielder Trey Nyoni, Arsenal winger Max Dowman and Norwich City's Jovon Makama are all hoping to earn their first caps.

Portugal will make at least three changes in the final third, a consequence of Carlos Forbs, Rodrigo Mora and Gustavo Varela not being named in this squad.

Olympiacos' Gustavo Sa should return in the number 10 role, Trabzonspor winger Noah Saviolo may feature on the flank and Augsburg's Rodrigo Ribeiro is in line to get the nod down the centre of the attack.

England Under-21s possible starting lineup:

Beadle; Norton-Cuffy, Phillips, Alleyne, Lewis; Gray; Nwaneri, Hinshelwood, Peck, George; Mubama

Portugal Under-21s possible starting lineup:

Ferreira; Banjaqui, Gabriel, Oliveira, Rego; De Amorim, Essugo; Saviolo, Sa, Moreira; Ribeiro

This has all the makings of a thrilling contest and England Under-21s are probably justified marginal favourites. However, Portugal also have an array of talent at this level, leading us to predict an away victory in a game full of goals.

#1842. Commentators haven't the foggiest idea what's going on: Thick mist ruins FA Cup clash for TV viewers - and fans use phone torches to see the action!

Published: 16:25 EST, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 16:27 EST, 7 November 2026

'Peak FA Cup', was the verdict from TV viewers watching (or trying to watch) the clash between Notts County and Altrincham as thick fog obscured the action.

Those tuning in on TNT Sports were baffled by what was actually happening in the game when the mist descended at Moss Lane.

Commentators saw the funny side, with Adam Summerton chuckling, saying: 'Your guess is as good as mine at the minute,' when asked by his partner what was going on.

As the match progressed, the foggy conditions only worsened and it became difficult for the players to see far in front of them, let alone those trying to spectate in the ground and at home.

Even though the conditions appeared to simply be deep fog, one local claimed it was smoke from local firework parties causing the white-out.

They wrote: 'It is smoke from the bonfire night fireworks and bonfires. I live round the corner, it is literally just smoke. All you can smell in the air is smoke.'

The fog is closing in at Moss Lane! 🌫️Conditions are getting tricky for Altrincham and Notts County 👀📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB pic.twitter.com/gTM9e3KA2w

Fog descended on the FA Cup clash between Altrincham and Notts County and TV viewers could hardly tell what was going on

Fans pulled out the torches on their phones in a light-hearted bid to see more of the action

Despite the lack of quality action for fans to watch at Moss Lane, plenty of them saw the funny side and even took out their phone torches in unison to try and cut through the gloom.

Those at home poked fun at the scene, with one posting: 'Can you ask the ref that if it goes to pens they bring the goal closer to the cameras so we can watch them?'

Another wrote: 'Where's the orange ball? I miss those days!'

Not everyone could see the humour in the situation, with one user on X writing: 'I'm sorry but this is ridiculous it should be abandoned. You could be miles offside.'

The game itself went to penalties, which caused further problems for the commentators, who had to largely base their reactions on the crowd directly behind the goal.

Ultimately, Notts County survived a scare from the non-league outfit and won 3-2 in the shootout.

Rosaire Longelo netted the final spot-kick to fire the Magpies into the second round of the FA Cup.

They'd had to fight back from 2-1 down in normal time after Lucas Weaver and then Lewis Banks put Altrincham in front.

Callum Roberts scored to make it 2-2 and neither side could find a winner in extra-time, meaning an already memorable game was settled in a fitting and dramatic fashion.

By Matt Law | 11 Nov 2026 10:54, Last updated: 11 Nov 2026 10:56

Moldova and Kazakhstan will continue their respective 2026-27 UEFA Nations League campaigns with a contest in Group C3 on Friday night.

Neither team can finish at the top of the section and secure automatic promotion to League B, but the pair are both in the running to qualify for the promotion playoffs.

Moldova have a record of one win, one draw and two defeats from their four matches in Group C3, with four points leaving them in third position in the table.

The Tricolours are level on points with second-placed Faroe Islands and will have their eyes on second spot, which would see them qualify for the promotion playoffs.

Lilian Popescu's side started their Group C3 campaign with a 2-0 loss to Slovakia, before drawing 1-1 with Faroe Islands ahead of a 2-1 victory over Kazakhstan.

Moldova will enter this match off the back of a 4-0 defeat to Slovakia, and they are now preparing for their final two games in the section against Kazakhstan and Faroe Islands.

The Tricolours have only actually won one match since November 2024, which proved to be their 2-1 success over Kazakhstan in the reverse game between the two sides.

As for Kazakhstan, a record of two draws and two defeats has left them at the bottom of Group C3 on two points, two points behind second-placed Faroe Islands.

The Hawks started their 2026-27 Nations League campaign with a 1-1 draw against Faroe Islands before suffering back-to-back losses to Slovakia and Moldova.

The Hawks will finish their Group C3 campaign at home to Slovakia on November 16.

#1840. England XI when record-breaker Harry Kane made his debut - where are they now?

Harry Kane is set to make even more England history tonight, with the Ballon d’Or winner just one appearance away from overtaking Peter Shilton as his country’s most-capped men’s footballer of all time.

Already the Three Lions’ record goalscorer with 91, Kane will reach 126 caps in the span of 11 years if he is selected by Thomas Tuchel to face Croatia in the Nations League at Wembley on Thursday night.

Kane was handed his senior England debut in a European Championship qualifier against Lithuania back in 2015, his maiden selection after impressing for Tottenham during the 2014/15 season.

Then aged 21, Kane had already grabbed 26 goals in 42 appearances for Spurs by March.

But that was not enough for Kane to be immediately named in the starting lineup by Roy Hodgson, instead coming on a substitute before scoring a debut goal just 79 seconds later.

Ahead of a record night at Wembley, Standard Sport looks at England’s starting lineup when Kane made his England debut.

Long-serving goalkeeper Joe Hart started against Lithuania, as to be expected during what was a period of relative stability between the sticks.

Understudies on the night included Jack Butland and Robert Green, but Hart was established as number one until 2017 - when the emergence of Jordan Pickford prevented him from earning more than 75 caps.

Retired in 2024 after a spell at Celtic and now works as a pundit on the BBC.

Nathaniel Clyne was never first-choice at right-back for Hodgson, with his 14 caps coming across a two-year period.

He managed to outlast Hodgson, but only picked up one more cap under Gareth Southgate. Currently without a club after his second stint at Crystal Palace ended in the summer.

Gary Cahill was enjoying the most consistent spell of his England career in 2015, a trusted centre-back after Rio Ferdinand and John Terry had both retired.

First called up by Fabio Capello, Cahill served under five different England managers in total - his last appearance coming under Southgate at the 2018 World Cup.

Ended his career at Bournemouth and retired in 2022. Now works in the media.

Handed a debut by Hodgson’s predecessor Capello, Phil Jones’ England career was impacted by the same issues as his spell at Manchester United - injuries.

How Harry Kane bucked every trend to become England's superstar

UK braced for first cold snap of season as temperatures set to plummet

Where to watch England vs Croatia: TV channel and live stream

Hodgson liked to include Jones in his team when fit, but he only made 27 appearances for England in total - his last cap coming in the third-place play-off at the 2018 World Cup in Russia.

After spells coaching at United and Blackburn after retiring in 2023, he is now first-team coach at Sheffield United.

Long-serving Everton left-back Leighton Baines had to wait to inherit the same position for the national team from Ashley Cole.

However, the emergence of Luke Shaw meant that the Lithuania game was Baines’ 30th and final cap for England.

He has coached at Everton since retiring in 2020 and currently serves as an assistant to manager David Moyes.

Now a veteran of over 450 Premier League games, 11 years ago Henderson was already established in the England midfield.

A foray in Saudi Arabia briefly halted his England career, but Henderson was still involved in the squad for the 2026 World Cup, making his 90th Three Lions appearance in the group stage game against Panama.

Signed for Chelsea in the summer after leaving Brentford and has become an important member of their midfield under Xabi Alonso, aged 36.

Once a promising Leeds youngster, Fabian Delph was making the fourth of just 20 appearances for England against Lithuania.

Delph’s international career received a brief resurgence under Southgate, used as a makeshift left-back after Pep Guardiola had converted the midfielder into a defender for Manchester City.

Retired in 2022 and has done some media work since then.

11 years ago Michael Carrick was coming to the end of a storied career that included Premier League and Champions League glory at Manchester United.

Already in the post-Sir Alex Ferguson era, United have since slid much further - with Carrick now set to be sacked from his role as head coach at Old Trafford after just one win in 10 Premier League games this term.

Raheem Sterling produced the assist for Kane’s debut England goal, and despite being only 20, the winger had already earned 13 caps.

Since breaking onto the scene as a teenager at Liverpool, Sterling reached new heights at City - before a harsh decline left the 31-year-old hunting for a club after a short stint at Feyenoord in the Netherlands. He has not played for England since 2022.

Like Henderson, veteran Danny Welbeck was signed by Chelsea in the summer to add experience to a young squad at Stamford Bridge.

Unlike his club team-mate, Welbeck has not enjoyed the same longevity with England. In fact, the Lithuania game was his last competitive start for the Three Lions, only earning nine more caps to bring his total tally to 42.

Rather fittingly, Kane replaced Wayne Rooney against Lithuania in the 71st minute - the man he would one day overtake as England’s top goalscorer.

Rooney’s England career never lived up to the expectations in terms of silverware, but his 53 goals in 120 games put ‘Wazza’ into the history books as his country’s top goalscorer and most-capped outfield player - before Kane took both records.

After spells in management at Derby, D.C. United, Birmingham and Plymouth, he is now thriving as a pundit.

#1839. Pictured: Michael Carrick arrives at Carrington before Manchester United sack meeting

Michael Carrick has been pictured arriving at Carrington for the final time as Manchester United manager.

The under-fire Man Utd boss gave a thumbs up as he was photographed driving into the car park at the club’s training base early on Thursday morning.

Carrick is expected to be sacked by United at Carrington later in the day in a face-to-face meeting with United’s CEO Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox, who are both now back in the UK following their crucial talks with co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe in Monaco on Wednesday.

It was decided in that summit after weeks of speculation that Carrick would be relieved of his duties after an abysmal start to the season that has seen United win only one of their first 10 Premier League games and sit in the relegation zone heading into the final international break of 2026.

United are believed to be lining up Mauricio Pochettino as Carrick’s replacement, with an official approach now understood to have been made to US Soccer and an agreement close on personal terms with a candidate they have spoken to on multiple occasions in the past and who is known to be keen on the role.

However, it remains to be seen when exactly Pochettino will take the reins at Old Trafford, with suggestions that he could yet remain in charge of the United States national team for their upcoming two-legged Concacaf Nations League quarter-final tie.

The USA play Haiti in Miami on Saturday, before facing the same opponents in Cincinnati in a match that takes place overnight Tuesday into Wednesday, UK time.

United’s first game back after the international break is away to rivals Liverpool at Anfield next Sunday (November 22), after which they travel to Sporting in the Champions League and then host Brentford during a hectic fixture list in the run-up to Christmas.

The USA are understood to be targeting Pep Guardiola as a potential replacement for Pochettino, who will cost $10million (£7.5m) to release from a contract that was only extended until 2030 following the World Cup on home soil in the summer.

It is reported that United will have to pay more to secure members of his backroom team, including long-time assistant Jesus Perez.

Guardiola has been out of work since ending his trophy-laden 10-year spell in charge at Manchester City at the end of last season and has already been offered one foray into international management with Italy, but turned it down.

#1838. PSG and Bayern Munich eye £85m Argentinian winger for summer 2027

By Axel Clody | 11 Nov 2026 11:00, Last updated: 11 Nov 2026 11:00

Paris Saint-Germain could turn to Portugal to strengthen their attack, with a player who made negative headlines in an incident involving Vinicius Jr of Real Madrid.

According to information relayed by Portuguese outlet Record, the French capital club are interested in Gianluca Prestianni, a young Argentine winger at Benfica.

Bayern Munich are also keeping an eye on his situation. The matter could gather pace in the coming months, even though the reported price tag gives pause for thought: close to £85m (€100m).

Prestianni’s name is not unknown to European football fans, but the forward was mostly at the centre of a fierce controversy last February. During the Champions League play-off between Benfica and Real Madrid, the Argentine was accused by Vinicius Jr of having racially abused him.

The Brazilian winger alerted the referee, leading to a brief interruption of the match. Prestianni denied the accusations. UEFA ultimately sanctioned the player with a six-match ban, three of them suspended, for homophobic behaviour.

Since that episode, the 20-year-old has been talked about more for his performances. This season, the Argentina international has particularly convincing numbers in Lisbon colours: he has already scored 12 goals and provided six assists in 20 appearances in all competitions for Benfica.

That return explains why several European heavyweights are starting to take an interest in his profile, including PSG.

Right-footed and able to play on both wings, Prestianni has interesting qualities in tight spaces. His dribbling, quickness and ability to take on his man one-on-one allow him to make a difference in the final metres.

PSG and Bayern Munich are therefore following a player whose stock is rising quickly. But Benfica do not intend to let him go at any price: his valuation could reach £85m (€100m).

A sum like that inevitably raises questions. Prestianni has obvious potential, but the Argentine has not yet shown he can maintain this level of play over several seasons at the highest European level. His current statistics are impressive, but they will need to be confirmed over time and against top-class opposition.

At PSG, his integration would not be straightforward either. There is heavy competition on the wings, notably Desire Doue, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, Maghnes Akliouche and Mika Godts.

To win a place in Luis Enrique’s starting XI, the Argentine would need to quickly offer more than a simple ability to beat his opponent. His work rate, his work without the ball and his consistency in attacking decisions would be decisive.

PSG have the means to position themselves for this type of talent, but spending £85m on a player who is still developing would be a risky investment. At that price, Prestianni should already be a safe bet, and not just a particularly appealing prospect.

However, it is not out of the question that the Benfica player could leave for a lower sum in the summer 2027 transfer window.

#1837. Key adjustments and becoming possession-oriented: Tactical analysis of Genoa 1-2 AC Milan

AC Milan climbed back into the top four in the Serie A table with a much-needed win away against Genoa before the international break.

Milan found themselves two goals up inside 20 minutes when Alphadjo Cisse slotted in a cut-back from Adrien Rabiot and Christian Pulisic buried a square pass from Gonçalo Ramos, with both goals coming from the high press.

However, it wouldn’t be the Rossoneri without some late drama, and Ellertsson made it a very nervy finish for the Rossoneri with a goal inside the final few minutes from a long-range strike. Milan did manage to hang on for what was an important three points.

Como’s defeat to Inter means that Ruben Amorim’s men move into the Champions League places, though after the break the pursuit of consistency will continue. Below is the tactical breakdown, from Rohit Rajeev.

Amorim chose to make five changes from Thursday’s defeat to Ferencvaros. Mike Maignan, Mario Gila, Luka Modric, Diego Moreira and Christian Pulisic all came into the side, though there were some question marks about whether it would be a four or three-man defence based on the names selected.

Genoa’s direct approach immediately put Milan on the back foot, with the hosts threatening to exploit the space behind the defensive line in the opening minute.

They played a long ball into the space behind Koni De Winter, allowing Osmanjic to run in behind and chase the delivery. Although the move appeared to be offside, it served as an early warning of the threat Genoa’s direct approach could pose to Milan’s defence.

Genoa anticipated Milan’s tendency to create numerical overloads in the wide areas and adjusted their defensive structure accordingly.

They used the corresponding centre-back, wing-back and both players from the double pivot to create a 4v3 numerical superiority against Milan’s wide combinations.

This allowed Genoa to outnumber Milan’s attacking players, restrict their progression down the flanks and make it difficult for Amorim’s side to exploit their usual wide overloads.

Milan’s in-possession structure alternated between a 4-1-4-1 and a 3-1-4-2, with the positioning of Musah largely determining which shape the team adopted.

Rabiot occupied the left half-space, while Pulisic preferred to operate closer to Moreira on the right. Meanwhile, Cisse provided the width on the left flank, functioning as Milan’s left winger.

Milan operated with a vertically staggered double pivot, comprising Modric and Rabiot. Modric occupied the deeper position, acting as the midfield screen in front of the back four and providing a link between defence and midfield.

Rabiot, meanwhile, operated higher up the pitch, effectively taking on the role of an attacking midfielder and providing an additional presence between Genoa’s midfield and defensive lines.

The move leading to Cisse’s goal began with Vasquez being tasked with progressing possession from the back. However, Milan managed to create a 3v4 numerical disadvantage for Genoa in the wide areas, forcing Vasquez to recycle possession rather than progress the ball.

Pulisic recognised the opportunity to press and initiated a ball-oriented press, eventually dispossessing Vasquez. He immediately released Rabiot, allowing Milan to exploit the turnover before Genoa could reorganise defensively.

As the possession changed hands, Ramos scanned his surroundings and identified Cisse’s position, recognising the opportunity to attack the space inside the penalty area.

Milan subsequently created a 3v2 numerical advantage inside the box. Cisse initially ran alongside Ramos before checking his run to deceive Marcandalli. This subtle change of movement created separation from his marker and allowed him to attack the space.

Rabiot delivered the cross into the penalty area, where Cisse was perfectly positioned to finish the move and give Milan the lead.

Although Milan adopted a high, man-oriented pressing structure, there were gaps that Genoa could exploit during their build-up. Musah, conscious of the possibility of Genoa creating a 2v1 situation, chose to stay closer to Diawara rather than move out to engage the ball carrier.

This left Ezhibue free to receive possession in the sizeable gap between Musah and Cisse, exposing a weakness in Milan’s pressing structure.

The move leading to Milan’s second goal began with Cisse pressing Traore from behind as the Genoa defender approached the goal line.

Under pressure, Traore attempted a cross-field pass, but Ramos positioned himself intelligently to block the passing lane towards Vasquez.

Rather than attempting to finish the move himself, Ramos showed excellent composure and unselfishly squared the ball into Pulisic’s path, despite Moreira also calling for the pass.

What made the assist particularly impressive was the Portuguese’s execution: he played a no-look pass, deceiving both the goalkeeper and the recovering defender about his intended target. Pulisic capitalised on the opportunity and converted the chance to double Milan’s advantage.

With each passing game Milan are moving into a pure possession-oriented team. In this sequence you can see Pulisic and Rabiot exchanging their positions to confuse their markers

With a 2-0 advantage, Milan shifted towards a more conservative approach, prioritising defensive stability over attacking progression. Amorim reorganised the side into a 5-4-1 defensive structure, adding greater protection to the backline and reducing the spaces available for Genoa to exploit.

However, one of the inherent vulnerabilities of a five-man defensive structure is the space left behind the wing-backs when they are drawn towards the ball.

Genoa looked to exploit this weakness by deliberately dragging Moreira out of his defensive position. As Moreira stepped forward to engage the ball carrier, Gila was forced to jump out of the defensive line to prevent Genoa from creating a 2v1 situation.

This movement consequently opened up space in the right channel, allowing Genoa to exploit an area that would otherwise have been protected by Milan’s compact 5-4-1 defensive block.

Genoa switched from their initial 3-4-2-1 to a 4-4-2 formation as they looked to change their attacking approach. El Shaarawy moved into the left midfield position, Vitinha operated on the right, while Baldanzi took up the role of a second striker.

The substitution of Marcandalli also prompted a structural change at the back, with Genoa abandoning their back three in favour of a back four. Ekhator moved into the right-back position, allowing Genoa to maintain a more conventional defensive structure.

For Genoa’s goal, Milan failed to close down Ellertsson, with the defenders seemingly anticipating a cross rather than a shot. Ellertsson recognised the opportunity and noticed that Maignan’s line of sight was obstructed by four Milan defenders.

Taking advantage of the goalkeeper’s limited visibility, he opted to shoot rather than deliver a cross, finding the back of the net.

Published: 17:03 EST, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 17:26 EST, 7 November 2026

Charlie Savage came out on top in the FA Cup's Battle of the Savages with a goal against his dad Robbie's new team, Peterborough United.

Already two goals up thanks to strikes by Daniel Kyerewaa and Jack Marriott, Reading made a place in round two virtually secure when Robbie's son Charlie added a third in first-half stoppage time.

The midfielder, 23, latched on to a loose ball on the edge of the Peterborough area and fired home, with the aid of a slight deflection, before racing off towards the visiting fans and celebrating with a knee slide.

Dad Robbie, who took over as Posh boss last month after his stint at Forest Green Rovers, looked initially frustrated at his team's defending but you almost sensed a smile given the identity of the goalscorer.

'Charlie Savage's goal is all about him seeing the danger, holding his run, letting it run across his body and finishing,' said former Reading midfielder Steve Sidwell on BBC Sport. 'Reading are deservedly in charge of the game, and Savage has been superb.'

Former Leicester midfielder and Wales international Robbie had feared as much in an exclusive interview with the Daily Mail before the first-round tie.

Charlie Savage scores against his dad Robbie’s side! 😳Reading make it 3-0 at Peterborough! 🔥📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB pic.twitter.com/RmMzxfNIzE

'Charlie Savege's goal is all about him seeing the danger, holding his run, letting it run across his body and finishing,' said former Reading midfielder Steve Sidwell

'It's going to be horrible,' he had said. 'Every time I watch my sons play, I'm anxious. I'm nervous. I want them to do well. If they give the ball away and the other team attack, I've got butterflies thinking, "Please don't score".

That particular wish took on a new meaning as his lad lined up to shoot with his left foot to strengthen Reading's vice-like grip on the tie.

Like his dad, Charlie came through Manchester United's youth ranks and made one first-team appearance, as a substitute at the age of 18 against Young Boys in the Champions League. It was an unforgettable night for Robbie, who was on co-commentary duty with a lump in his throat.

Peterborough can now focus on improving their position from third bottom of League One, while Reading may wish to put thoughts of Wembley to one side as they set their sights on a promotion push.

#1834. Man United transfer news: New rival emerges in race for Alejandro Balde

By Axel Clody | 11 Nov 2026 11:14

AS Monaco could make a good move in the winter transfer market for a player who could leave Barcelona but who is also attracting interest from some big names, notably in the Premier League.

According to Sport, the Principality club are interested in Alejandro Balde, Barcelona’s left-back, whose future could be written away from Catalonia as early as next January.

It is a £34m (€40m) opportunity that is likely to appeal to Monaco, but the deal looks particularly complicated: several Premier League sides, as well as Italian clubs, are also in the running.

According to the Spanish outlet, Barcelona no longer rule out a departure for their 23-year-old defender. His agent, Jorge Mendes, has started sounding out the market to identify the options available to his client.

Monaco are among the suitors, but will have to contend with the ambitions of Liverpool, Manchester United, Manchester City, Tottenham Hotspur and Aston Villa. Roma and Juventus are also watching the situation.

A product of La Masia, Balde seemed destined for an important future at Barcelona.

A Spain international, the defender had established himself as a regular starter at left-back, thanks in particular to his athletic qualities and his ability to make a difference down his flank. But his situation has changed considerably under Hansi Flick.

Competition has increased and his playing time has melted away this season: Balde has played only 124 minutes in the league and the Champions League. It is a demotion that is hard to accept for a young player who still needs to play regularly to continue his progress.

Barcelona have therefore set their starting price at around £34m (€40m). It is a significant sum, but one that could allow the Catalan club to free up cash and reduce their wage bill, with the aim of strengthening their central defence in particular - an ambitious option has been reactivated, with Jonathan Tah of Bayern Munich.

For Balde, a loan with an option to buy, potentially obligatory under certain conditions, is also possible.

For Monaco, the interest is obvious. The left-back has a particularly sought-after profile: quick, capable of making repeated runs in behind and providing real attacking overload.

In a team that is looking to establish its game in the opposition half, his qualities could be valuable. The Spaniard could also regain a starting role and far more playing time than he currently has at Barcelona.

However, Monaco are not alone in this matter. The Premier League appears to be a particularly credible destination for the Spanish left-back. Liverpool, Manchester United, Manchester City, Tottenham and Aston Villa have all been sounded out by Mendes.

These clubs have greater financial resources than Monaco and can offer a particularly attractive sporting environment.

Roma and Juventus represent two other serious rivals. The Rome club are notably studying the possibility of a paid loan with an obligation to buy, conditional on qualification for next season’s Champions League. The player’s salary, however, is a financial obstacle for the Italian sides.

Monaco can nevertheless make one argument: the prospect of an important role from the moment he arrives, and the example of Ansu Fati, who relaunched himself well in the Principality last year. But between the financial demands of the Catalan club, Balde’s wages and the interest of several European heavyweights, Monaco will need to find the right arguments.

The move would be very interesting from a sporting point of view, but it remains to be seen whether they can convince the player to choose Ligue 1 over the Premier League or Serie A.

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Luis de la Fuente has reacted furiously to suggestions that Lamine Yamal enjoys extra privileges in the Spain camp, saying the "lies" to the contrary have hurt him.

Yamal will miss Spain's trip to Czechia on Thursday, having sustained a minor knee injury during Barcelona's 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid last weekend.

While De la Fuente confirmed on Wednesday that Yamal is expected to return to training on Friday, with a view to being available for Sunday's meeting with England, pundits in Spain have queried whether the winger receives special treatment from his head coach.

"Lamine suffered an injury and felt discomfort in his knee. He went for the usual treatment, and they discovered fluid in the knee and inflammation. That required rest," the Roja's World Cup-winning boss told reporters.

"Our medical staff, in coordination with his medical staff and I, decided that the best thing was for him to stay at home and train with his club, and to join us on Friday.

"We would have done the same thing with any other player. It does not bother me. We miss all the players who are not with us. This is football, and these are injuries.

#1832. Manchester United sack Michael Carrick with Mauricio Pochettino appointment close

Michael Carrick has officially been sacked by Manchester United after less than six months as the club’s permanent manager, with Mauricio Pochettino expected to replace him.

In a statement released on Thursday, United said that the club “has come to the extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary in order to achieve our ambitions” after a “disappointing start to the season” and that they “intend to appoint a permanent successor as quickly as possible”.

United added in tribute to Carrick: “Michael is, and always will be, a Manchester United legend. Just as he did as a player, he has conducted himself with the highest standards of dedication and professionalism throughout his time back with the club.

“His leadership and achievements last season will always be fondly remembered.”

Carrick took over as United’s interim head coach in January after Ruben Amorim’s departure and was promoted to the full-time job in May after qualifying for the Champions League last season.

He has failed to carry that momentum into the new campaign, though, and departs with United mired in the Premier League relegation zone having won only one of their first 10 matches and sitting 17th in the Champions League table. They also exited the Carabao Cup at the third round stage.

A 4-1 defeat by Como in Europe last month left Carrick on the brink and a 3-0 home loss to Bournemouth then initially looked as though it would be the end of the road, but he was spared the sack and retained for the visit to Chelsea, which the Red Devils lost 2-0.

A dramatic 3-2 comeback victory over Roma in the Champions League last week looked to restore some faith - at least temporarily - but a topsy-turvy performance against Aston Villa in a chaotic 4-4 draw, only salvaged at the death by Patrick Dorgu’s last-gasp equaliser, further underlined his side’s significant issues heading into the final international break of 2026.

United parted ways with Carrick following a meeting with director of football Jason Wilcox and CEO Omar Berrada held at Carrington, where, despite the intense speculation over his position, Carrick had continued to take training this week with United’s players not currently away on international duty.

Wilcox and Berrada had been in Monaco on Wednesday for crunch talks with United co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe, who controls the club’s sporting policy, where it was decided that a change in the dugout was needed to turn around their fortunes.

Pochettino is expected to replace Carrick and become the new manager at Old Trafford, despite only signing a four-year contract extension to remain in charge of the United States national team following the World Cup on home soil in the summer.

An official approach is believed to have been made to US Soccer, with Pochettino’s deal containing a release clause worth $10million (£7.5m). Pochettino is keen on the move and has spoken to United about their managerial position on multiple occasions in the past, with an agreement over personal terms reported to have been reached.

Former Chelsea and Tottenham boss Pochettino - who has seen off competition for the job from the likes of ex-Newcastle manager Eddie Howe and former Germany coach Julian Nagelsmann - would become United’s eighth permanent manager since Sir Alex Ferguson retired in 2013.

#1831. GdS: ‘Ahead of the curve’ – Amorim’s positive start compared to predecessors

Ruben Amorim might not have unanimously won everyone over yet, but AC Milan are off to their best Serie A start in four years.

La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) write this morning that Milan under Amorim have started better than under Massimiliano Allegri in 2025-26, Paulo Fonseca in 2024-25 and even Stefano Pioli’s final season in 2023-24.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The best start belongs to the coach who delivered the Scudetto though, with 31 points in the first eleven rounds of the 2021-22 season, which ended with the most recent Italian league title added to the trophy cabinet.

Amorim has also hit the ground running, with an average that, in previous seasons, would have placed him even higher. A year ago, with 24 points at this same stage of the tournament, Milan would have been the league leaders.

The numbers don’t lie: 24 out of a possible 33 points – garnered through seven wins, three draws, and only one Serie A defeat – amount to 2.18 points per match. By comparison, Allegri had reached 22 points, Fonseca 17 and Pioli also had 22 in his final year.

The coach behind the 2021-22 Scudetto also started with great momentum in the previous season (26 points in 2022-23) and in the 2020-21 campaign (27 points).

These figures were double the 13 points from the 2019–20 season, a campaign that began with Marco Giampaolo at the helm, only for him to be replaced mid-season by Pioli. While still seeking to find that same rhythm in Europe, Milan have been surging in the league.

They got off to a blistering start with wins away at Torino and in their San Siro debut against Venezia, followed by a draw at Juventus – a match in which they were pegged back just minutes from the end -and another stalemate away to Lazio.

After falling two goals behind, Milan fought back against the team currently leading the league. Given Lazio’s subsequent form, that result takes on added significance. Next came a victory over Lecce, followed by a lacklustre draw in Reggio Emilia against Sassuolo.

From that point on, the turning point arrived: four wins in the next five matches, including away victories against Udinese and Genoa away from home, as well as the derby. The only stumble during this stretch was against Bologna.

Sensing that the squad was under significant stress, Amorim has granted a week off, with training set to resume next Monday. For those without other commitments such as international duty, this provides a chance to truly switch off.

Many players have headed away, while those who remained are either following strict injury recovery programs or simply taking a break. This pause is longer than usual: the typical break in professional leagues is generally shorter.

This isn’t the only unusual aspect: the return to training ahead of the match against Frosinone the following week will also take place only after the players returning from international duty have been given ample time to rest.

There are precedents for this, though. For instance, the team was given a Tuesday off just two days before their European away match against Bournemouth. They returned to the pitch on Wednesday, the same day they departed for England. The result was a 3-0 loss and a dark night.

There is certainly enough evidence now to speak of new methods introduced by Amorim and his staff. On the pitch, Rúben has brought in new ideas: training sessions are never overly gruelling, and the data from GPS trackers and distance-monitoring tools is never pushed to ‘excessive’ levels.

“We train by playing,” the Portuguese coach has often explained, implying that matches themselves offer the best opportunities to test tactical schemes and movements. This is especially the case when playing every three days, with such little time between games.

While this approach may have initially raised some eyebrows among the players and was even speculated to be a cause for the cluster of injuries the Rossoneri experienced, such concerns were dispelled once the coach provided further clarification.

In the meantime, no one is taking a break fully. Even while away, every player has been assigned specific training programs to follow, ensuring they return in peak condition to keep the good league form going.

England and Croatia return to UEFA Nations League action on Thursday night.

The two teams are competing in Group 3 of League A as they bid to bolster their hopes in this competition and their chances of Euro 2028 qualification.

Here, Sports Mole provides details of how to tune into the contest.

The Nations League match will kick off at 7.45pm, UK time, on Thursday.

England against Spain will take place at Wembley Stadium, which boasts a capacity of 90,000

This is the first time that England have squared off against Croatia at this particular venue since their opening match of Euro 2020, which was held in June 2021.

The Nations League match will be shown live on ITV1 and STV for viewers in the UK.

ITV's streaming service ITVX will be showing the Nations League match from Wembley live, and it can be accessed on phones, computers and games consoles.

In Scotland, the STV Player will provide similar levels of access.

Action from the game will be uploaded to the ITV Sport YouTube channel and itv.com shortly after the full-time whistle at Wembley Stadium.

The @itvfootball X account will also post goals, red cards and other notable incidents.

When England lost to Spain on matchday one, Thomas Tuchel would have accepted that they needed four successive victories to remain in the hunt for top spot.

Not only have the Three Lions recorded three wins in a row, their 7-0 triumph in Croatia has essentially ensured that England will finish second in a worst-case scenario.

There is currently a 21-goal difference between England and Croatia in the table. For Croatia to remain as contenders for the runners-up spot, they must win by at least a 7-0 scoreline at Wembley.

Realistically-speaking, Croatia will be focused on avoiding relegation to League B of the UEFA Nations League. That would be achieved if they can avoid defeat at Wembley and Spain beat Czech Republic.

#1829. Tuchel not eyeing club return amid Pochettino Man Utd links

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Thomas Tuchel insists he will not leave the England job to take any offer in club football before Euro 2028, amid reports that Mauricio Pochettino is set to leave the United States for Manchester United.

On Wednesday, widespread reports suggested Pochettino – who has been in charge of the USMNT since 2024 – was set to quit his role and join United.

The Red Devils are set to sack Michael Carrick after entering the international break 18th in the Premier League table, the first time they have sat in the relegation zone this far into a season since 1986-87.

And ahead of England facing Croatia and Spain in the Nations League, that impending move led reporters to ask how Tuchel sees his future.

In February, the German penned a two-year contract extension to cover England's home campaign at Euro 2028.

He attracted stern criticism following the Three Lions' World Cup semi-final defeat to Argentina in July, but the Football Association reiterated its commitment to him after the tournament.

Asked if he had a release clause or would push for an exit for the right opportunity, Tuchel said: "There's no release clause, and there's no intention.

"I signed the contract – I want to stay until the Euros. I want to do the Euros. We have unfinished business."

Asked if he could guarantee he would not leave his current job, even if one of Europe's top clubs came calling, Tuchel replied: "Yeah, I would say so."
