By Matt Law | 11 Nov 2026 11:29, Last updated: 11 Nov 2026 11:31

Switzerland will be bidding to secure first spot in Group B1 and automatic promotion to League A when they continue their UEFA Nations League campaign on Friday against Slovenia.

National Team have been perfect in the 2026-27 tournament, collecting 12 points from four matches, and they will be facing a Slovenia side that are second in the section.

Slovenia boast a record of two wins, one draw and one defeat from their four matches in Group B1, with seven points representing a solid return.

Bostjan Cesar's side are three points ahead of third-placed Scotland and five behind the leaders Switzerland, demonstrating the need for them to secure a win on Friday night.

Slovenia, as it stands, are in a promotion playoff spot, but they could still finish first or third, with two games left to play, heading to North Macedonia after this one.

The hosts picked up four points from their first two games in the section, drawing 0-0 with Scotland before recording a 2-0 win over North Macedonia; a 2-1 defeat to Switzerland followed, and they then recorded a 2-1 victory over Scotland last time out.

Slovenia have only won two of their previous 12 matches against Switzerland in all competitions, with their last success over Friday's opponents coming in October 2014.

Switzerland are certain of a top-two spot in the section, but it would be a shock if they passed up first position and automatic promotion to League A from such a strong position.

National Team are top of Group B1 on 12 points, and they have been impressive in the tournament, opening up with a 3-0 win over North Macedonia, before recording a 3-0 victory over Scotland in their second away game in the section.

Murat Yakin's side then won back-to-back home fixtures in October, beating Slovenia 2-1 and North Macedonia 3-0 to take complete control of the section.

Switzerland were beaten by Argentina in the quarter-finals of the 2026 World Cup, but they have won eight of their last nine matches and will once again be the favourites here.

National Team will finish their Group B1 campaign at home to Scotland on November 16.

Slovenia will be without the services of two players through suspension on Friday, with David Zec and Erik Janza missing due to an accumulation of yellow cards.

Benjamin Sesko is another notable absentee for the home side; the Manchester United striker remains unavailable with a shin injury and is not expected back until early 2027.

Swansea City's Zan Vipotnik started through the middle against Scotland last time out, and the 24-year-old is expected to keep hold of his spot in the XI for this match.

Switzerland, meanwhile, have no suspension issues, although a booking for Michel Aebischer in this match would see him ruled out of the team's final group fixture.

There are not expected to be any major surprises in the away side's lineup for this match, with Remo Freuler, Johan Manzambi and Dan Ndoye among those set to be in the starting side.

Meanwhile, there should be a spot through the middle for Zeki Amdouni, who has scored 14 times in 37 appearances for his country.

#1825. ST MIRREN 0 RANGERS 2: It's back to the grind for McInnes' men as they show grit to see off Buddies

By KEVIN MCKENNA AT MARBILL COACHES STADIUM

Published: 17:42 EST, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 17:51 EST, 7 November 2026

At some stage, you would suspect Rangers are going to find their groove under Derek McInnes.

But until then, they will happily settle for just getting points on the board. How they go about it doesn’t really matter in the grand scheme of things.

This hard-fought victory in Paisley — much like so many of Rangers’ Premiership wins this season — was all about substance over style.

Yes, there were flashes of quality here and there. But it was more to do with doing the ugly stuff well than anything else. Fortunately for McInnes, his side are proving to be adept at doing so.

It’s a handy habit to have at their disposal. We saw it in recent draws at Dundee and Hearts last month, managing to come away with something when they probably deserved nothing.

With nobody knowing what version of Celtic are going to turn up on any given week, all Rangers can do is stay within touching distance of the league leaders — a point in front ahead of their meeting with Kilmarnock this afternoon — until they come to blows again in the new year.

Rangers skipper Neil nets with the aid of a deflection to put his side two goals up

Rangers wasted no time getting themselves on the front foot. St Mirren barely got a kick in the opening exchanges, and on the odd occasion they did, possession was turned over far too easily.

Badredine Bouanani had the visitors’ first effort of the night on six minutes, cutting inside from the right flank before pulling the trigger from 20 yards, but it lacked the power to properly test Jacob Chapman in the Saints goal.

The keeper had to be far more alert five minutes later, pulling off a wonderful reaction stop to deny Ryan Naderi finishing off Kevin Kelsy’s headed knockdown. You would have put your house on the in-form Czech finding the net.

Emmanuel Fernandez headed over from the resulting corner.

Having finally settled down, St Mirren gave their opponents a perfect opportunity to take the lead, when Samuel Ramos brought down James Penrice on the angle of the Buddies’ box.

There didn’t appear to be a great deal of contact, but it didn’t take long for VAR to confirm referee Nick Walsh’s decision.

Naderi stepped up to do what he failed to do moments earlier, coolly slotting into the bottom corner to register his ninth goal in all competitions this season.

From looking as if he was likely to be on his way out of Ibrox over the summer, the 23-year-old has become one of the first names on McInnes’ team sheet.

Penrice goes down under Ramos' challenge to earn Rangers a penalty in the first half

And perhaps the most exciting thing from a Rangers perspective is that he is still a million miles from being the finished article. But playing with this sort of confidence, he’s only going to get better.

He was involved in a lovely free-flowing counter shortly after the half-hour mark, with the ball eventually falling to Kim Min-su on the penalty spot. However, the South Korean delayed getting his shot off and the chance was gone.

When running full-flight at defences, the 20-year-old is a delight to watch in that No10 role.

There isn’t anyone in the country better at finding pockets of space between the lines and taking the ball on the turn. But for all that there is to enjoy about his game, his decision-making in the key moments undoubtedly needs work.

A woeful ball out from Olwethu Makhanya set up a two-v-two for the hosts before the break, with Ramos drilling straight at Ivor Pandur from inside the area. With the whole goal to aim at, the Spaniard should have done much better.

The same goes for Jake Young, who blasted high and wide from a promising position a minute later.

Naderi is hailed by Min-su after putting the visitors ahead from the spot

As dominant as Rangers were, you never got the feeling their lead was particularly secure, such is their tendency to play themselves into trouble every now and then.

Fernandez is the worst culprit for it. Fortunately for him, his recovery pace gets him out of jail more often than not. He needed it on a couple of occasions here.

A delightful threaded ball from Bouanani found the feet of Min-su inside the box on 47 minutes but under heavy pressure, he was unable to prod beyond Chapman who’d rushed off his line to meet him. It was hard to be too critical of the Rangers midfielder this time.

Chapman was once again called into action to thwart Kelsy from close range after the Venezuelan escaped the clutches of his marker to collect Min-su’s pass in behind.

He then skewed an effort wide at the back post from an excellent Nico Raskin delivery from the right. It was a night on which very little came off for the big man in front of goal.

To his credit, he kept plugging away, and played a key role in Rangers’ doubling their advantage just after the hour mark, with his driving run causing a bit of chaos in the Buddies backline, before captain Dan Neil swept a loose ball into the bottom corner via the aid of a big deflection to give Chapman absolutely no chance of saving.

With his first touch, substitute Eseosa Sule wasted a glorious chance to reduce the deficit after being left all alone at the back post to stab home Declan John’s cross.

With the ball seemingly destined for the back of the net, Rangers keeper Pandur produced a stunning save on the stretch to turn the ball round the post.

The Croatian’s signing went somewhat under the radar over the summer, but he has demonstrated time and time again that he is a man for the big occasion. He’ll win this side plenty of points between now and the end of the season.

McInnes applauds the away support after signing off for the international break with a win

St Mirren came into this one having won just once in their past eight, but you wouldn’t have guessed they were struggling for confidence given the way in which they threw everything at the game in an effort to get a result.

It wasn’t for lack of trying, with Luke Thomas testing Pandur from range before Calvin Ramsay’s follow-up header clipped the post.

That would be as close as Saints would come, as Rangers dug in to grind out an ugly — but ultimately deserved — win on the road.

They will need to be far better, far more consistently if they want to get their hands on the Premiership title come May. But that’s a worry for another day.

Alphadjo Cisse is attracting interest after his red-hot start to the season, and AC Milan are already rejecting advances.

“Milan are rejecting verbal offers from several clubs. Milan are already saying no to several clubs for Cisse. There are several Premier League clubs, and I’ll name one, Brighton,” the journalist began.

Milan paid €8m, having tried to sign him in previous years from Verona Primavera. Congratulations to Milan and to all the management linked to Cisse.”

#1823. Prediction: Egypt vs Malawi

Getting their AFCON qualifying adventure back underway on Friday night, Egypt will welcome Malawi to Cairo.

While Europe’s elite domestic leagues might be in the midst of November’s international break, there are plenty of attractive betting promotions available.

Starting with the hosts, getting October underway with a toothless 1-0 friendly defeat against South Africa, Egypt are searching for an immediate response when they reignite their AFCON qualifying charge this weekend. Nevertheless, despite getting their Group B adventure underway with an uneventful 0-0 stalemate at home against Angola on September 25th, the Pharaohs did put a maiden qualifying victory on the board against South South Sudan. Signing off September with a routine 5-0 romp on foreign soil, Ali Maher’s side will be seeking a repeat performance on Friday night. Suffering an infamous World Cup collapse back in July as they watched their North American adventure come to an end thanks to a rollercoaster 3-2 loss against Argentina, Egypt are searching for some recent stability. In fact, Maher’s camp have registered just a single win from any of their previous six appearances across all competitions within 90 minutes.

Completing a blockbuster summer switch to Turkish outfit Trabzonspor and already registering 12 direct goal contributions in his first 11 domestic appearances this season (nine goals, three assists), former Liverpool icon Mohamed Salah will lead Egypt out in Cairo.

Likewise, making an initial season-long loan switch to Tottenham, Omar Marmoush will partner Salah in the final third and complete an all-star attack. Completing a permanent move to Scottish giants Celtic, Haissem Hassan has been included in Maher’s maiden squad.

As for the visitors, while Malawi might have opened their respective AFCON qualifying campaign with a 2-1 victory at home against South Sudan on September 25th, Callisto Pasuwa’s side immediately came crashing back down to earth last time out. Getting October underway with a routine 3-1 loss at the hands of Angola, Friday’s guests will be bracing themselves for a monumental challenge when they travel to Cairo this weekend. Registering just a sole competitive win so far this calendar year, Malawi will also be concerned by a nightmare record against Egypt. Hit with a 4-0 drumming when they last met the Pharaohs for an AFCON qualifying showdown back in March 2023, they have lost each of their previous three straight meetings by an aggregate score of 8-1. It should also be highlighted, Pasuwa’s camp have mustered just a single competitive victory on foreign soil over the past 20 months.

The likes of Innocent Nyasulu, Nixon Nyasulu and Lanjesi Nkhoma have all received recalls to Malawi’s squad this month. Arguably the most notable name in Pasuwa’s squad and making a maiden Bundesliga 2 appearance for Hannover prior to November’s international break, 19-year-old Mwisho Mhango will feature in Cairo.

Former Sherif Tiraspol midfielder Charles Pietro will lead Malawi out on Friday night. Appearing to have cemented his spot as Pasuwa’s number one choice, William Thole should keep his spot between the sticks this weekend.

Putting a maiden AFCON qualifying victory on the board as they signed off September with a dominant 5-0 victory away at South Sudan, Egypt will be seeking a repeat performance here. While the African heavyweights might be searching for some recent stability, they have certainly been handed a golden opportunity this weekend. Rightfully installed as a landslide contender when they return to Cairo on Friday night, Egypt also hold a dominant record against Malawi. Landing a routine 4-0 win when they last met Malawi back in March 2023, we are expecting a similar outcome.

#1822. Manchester United drop clear hint over next manager move as timeline emerges

Manchester United have announced the departure of Michael Carrick - and immediately pledged to “appoint a permanent successor as quickly as possible”, with Mauricio Pochettino waiting in the wings.

Carrick was relieved of his duties as Man Utd boss on Thursday morning during a face-to-face meeting with CEO Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox, held at the club’s Carrington training base.

The decision to remove Carrick was made on Wednesday, when Berrada and Wilcox travelled to Monaco for talks with United co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe.

In a statement to confirm his exit, United wrote: “After a disappointing start to the season, the club has come to the extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary in order to achieve our ambitions.

“Michael is, and always will be, a Manchester United legend. Just as he did as a player, he has conducted himself with the highest standards of dedication and professionalism throughout his time back with the club.

“His leadership and achievements last season will always be fondly remembered. The club intends to appoint a permanent successor as quickly as possible.”

Carrick was initially handed a stay of execution after a dismal 3-0 defeat at home to Bournemouth last month that followed immediately after a heavy 4-1 away loss to Como in the Champions League.

Amid more heavy speculation over his future, Carrick was left in post for United’s trip to Chelsea the following weekend - which they lost 2-0 despite an improved first-half display.

Carrick’s short permanent tenure showed brief signs of life in a comeback against Roma - a 3-2 win that ended a run of nine winless games across all competitions - before twice hitting back from a two-goal deficit to draw 4-4 at home to Aston Villa in what proved to be his final game in charge.

Carrick led training on Tuesday and Wednesday at Carrington with the United players not currently away on international duty, despite reports that he was in line to be sacked.

United are expected to swiftly appoint Pochettino as Carrick’s replacement, having now made an official approach to US Soccer as they look to trigger the $10million (£7.5m) clause that would release him from a four-year contract extension that was only signed in the summer following the World Cup on home soil.

It has been suggested that United are comfortable with Pochettino taking charge of the USA’s two upcoming Concacaf Nations League quarter-final matches against Haiti during the current international window.

Pochettino’s first game as United head coach could still come away at Anfield, with the Red Devils facing fierce rivals Liverpool on Sunday, November 22.

Their statement to sack Carrick appears to confirm that they will not consider another interim or caretaker appointment, which is how Carrick returned to the club in January after Ruben Amorim’s exit.

#1821. South Africa vs Kenya - prediction, team news, lineups

By Byron David | 11 Nov 2026 11:42

South Africa will look to continue their post-World Cup momentum when they host Kenya in an Africa Cup of Nations qualifier on Friday, November 13, at the Orlando Stadium in Johannesburg.

With the visitors already guaranteed a spot in next year's tournament as co-hosts, only one slot is open for qualification in Group D.

South Africa are coming off what was their best-ever display at a World Cup, as they progressed from the group to the knockouts for the first time in their history.

Bafana Bafana seem to be riding that wave of success, as they have won both of their opening AFCON qualifiers in the group.

The men in green and gold have achieved positive results from excellent performances, despite a huge change in their technical team.

Hugo Broos stepped down from his role, opening the door for Pitso Mosimane to return to the helm for his second stint as the national coach.

The players have responded positively to Mosimane, as they are unbeaten under his guidance during his second tenure, with South Africa beating Egypt last time out in an international friendly.

The 1996 AFCON champions are also the most potent side in the qualifying roster, scoring seven goals in two games at an average of 3.5 goals per match.

Having been unbeaten in their only two head-to-heads with Kenya, the hosts are expected to secure three points here and consolidate their position at the top of Group D.

Kenya are currently led by former South African forward Benni McCarthy, who is dealing with salary payment issues with his current employers.

Nonetheless, he has stated that he will maintain his professionalism and lead the Harambee Stars to Johannesburg this week.

The visitors have their work cut out for them, especially since they are winless in their opening two fixtures of qualifying, drawing their opener with Eritrea and losing their recent competitive fixture against Guinea.

Their results here have no bearing on their qualification, as they will feature in the 2027 AFCON as co-hosts; however, McCarthy still wants his men to gather momentum in preparation for their home tournament.

Kenya have not scored in five of their last 10 matches, while they failed to bother the scorers in their previous two meetings with South Africa.

McCarthy will have to improve his team's form up front if they are to cause the hosts any issues on Friday.

#1820. Aston Villa transfer news: Unai Emery favourite 'signs new deal' until 2032

By Darren Plant | 11 Nov 2026 11:53, Last updated: 11 Nov 2026 11:55

Aston Villa have reportedly agreed a new long-term contract with Ian Maatsen.

In recent weeks, it has become an open secret that Unai Emery is negotiating fresh terms to remain in the Villa Park dugout past 2029.

While Villa chiefs were seemingly reacting to potential interest from Manchester United, Emery has also publicly reiterated his commitment to the West Midlands outfit.

Earlier this week, Villa also made progress on the playing side by activating a 12-month option in the contract of Victor Lindelof.

That was reward for the Sweden international becoming a mainstay in the centre of Emery's defence during 2026-27.

As per transfer expert Fabrizio Romano, Villa have also moved to extend the contract of Maatsen, with a formal announcement seemingly expected.

Romano says that the left-back has agreed to pen a deal that runs until the end of 2031-32.

At a time when the 24-year-old is not necessarily guaranteed regular starts when Matteo Ruggeri is fit, it is a major commitment from both parties.

Maatsen has contributed three goals and four assists from 100 appearances since his arrival from Chelsea in the summer of 2024.

With Maatsen already on terms until 2030, Villa did not necessarily need to hold any discussions with the Netherlands international.

At the same time, Maatsen's regular availability has proven important, and Emery will see him as a reliable member of the squad.

However, despite Maatsen impressing in the 2-1 victory over Manchester City last month, he did not feature in Villa's other two Premier League wins this season.

#1819. CM: Milan begin initial discussions over renewal for Musah – the situation

Yunus Musah has been one of the surprises of the season for AC Milan. Now, the management have begun talks over his contract.

Calciomercato.com begin a report on Musah by recalling what Sky pundit Alessandro Florenzi – a former Milan player himself – said to the midfielder live on air after the Rossoneri’s derby win over Inter.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

“I congratulate you because you’ve had two difficult years. I know you’re a guy who’s suffered a lot, but you’ve never given up,” the former full-back said.

“I can assure you of this because I’ve watched you work together for years. It’s truly been a great pleasure, so congratulations, and don’t get too big for your boots, but I’m sure you won’t because you’re a good guy.”

These were sincere words from someone who has experienced the Milan dressing room and knows how difficult it can be to succeed.

One of the key figures behind Musah’s new-found form is Ruben Amorim. The Portuguese coach completely revitalised him after two very difficult seasons, relying on him from day one and receiving a lot of hard work and dedication in return.

Amorim’s vision demands a player with Musah’s characteristics: a powerful engine, a remarkable ability to transform a passive game into an active one, and excellent transition skills. Versatility helps too, given that against Genoa the manager even deployed him as a left-back.

Musah’s season so far has seen him make 11 league appearances, with a total of 759 minutes played, plus three in the Europa League, with 222 minutes played. Going into preseason, that kind of reliance seemed impossible.

It’s not just Amorim who’s satisfied with Musah’s performances but the entire management as well, so much so that in recent days they’ve even discussed the possibility of extending his contract, which expires in 2028.

Recent contacts with the player’s entourage have helped them begin evaluating the possibility of renewing his deal. Musah currently earns around €2m per season and – if he maintains this level – he will sign new terms before the end of the season.

#1817. Angry Manchester United fans react to Michael Carrick sacking as new statement sent

The Manchester United Supporters Trust (MUST) have hit out at the club’s owners after Michael Carrick’s sacking marked another “depressing moment” at Old Trafford.

Carrick was relieved of his duties on Thursday morning, with United sitting 18th in the Premier League table after one win from their opening 10 matches.

It is expected that Mauricio Pochettino will be appointed as his replacement, though the timing of that has been complicated slightly by it being an international break and the USA preparing for two important Concacaf Nations League quarter-final matches against Haiti.

Confirmation of Carrick’s sacking came after United CEO Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox flew to Monaco on Wednesday to meet with co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe.

The MUST paid tribute to Carrick, who won five Premier League titles with United as a player, as the group instead took aim at Ratcliffe and the club’s majority owners, the Glazers.

“Michael Carrick’s departure marks another depressing moment for Manchester United,” an MUST statement read.

“We thank him for his service and for restoring hope during the second half of last season. His standing among supporters remains undiminished.

“The reason Manchester United fans have continued to support Michael Carrick in recent weeks is that they know that responsibility for United’s problems do not primarily rest with him or indeed his predecessors as manager.

“They lie with the ownership. The Glazers’ debt-funded takeover continues to burden the club. When INEOS came in they promised sporting excellence, but yet with repeated changes in football leadership we have seen anything but.”

The United fans had continued to stick with Carrick, even as results collapsed in recent weeks.

After the 3-0 defeat at home by Bournemouth last month, the Stretford End sung Carrick’s name as he made his way off the pitch.

“The earlier Stretford End banner declaring, ‘The way you treat us is a disgrace’ was a warning,” the MUST continued in their criticism of ownership.

“The unprecedented scale of the booing at Old Trafford, alongside public criticism from senior players in recent weeks, now points to a deeper deterioration.

“These are signs of a club becoming more divided, with the bond between supporters, players and those running Manchester United under increasing strain.”

No senior figures at United put their name to the official statement confirming Carrick’s sacking.

The MUST urged United executives to put greater emphasis on accountability to help improve the relationship between fans and those running the club.

By Matt Law | 11 Nov 2026 12:20, Last updated: 11 Nov 2026 12:23

Manchester United have reportedly reached an agreement in principle with Mauricio Pochettino to become their next head coach, should Michael Carrick be sacked.

The club's director of football Jason Wilcox and CEO Omar Berrada are meeting with co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe in Monaco on Wednesday to discuss Carrick's future at the helm.

The expectation is that Wilcox and Berrada will recommend Carrick is removed from his position as head coach due to the team's ongoing struggles.

Eddie Howe, Antonio Conte and Julian Nagelsmann have all been strongly linked with the position in recent weeks.

However, USA head coach Pochettino has now emerged as the red-hot favourite.

According to Sky Sports News, Man United have now come to an agreement with the Argentine over the managerial role at Old Trafford, should Carrick be sacked.

The report claims that the 20-time English champions are willing to pay the £7.4m required to release Pochettino from his contract with the United States.

Meanwhile, the club are also said to be prepared to pay compensation in order to ensure that Pochettino can bring his trusted staff members with him to Old Trafford.

Pochettino has a contract with the United States until the end of the 2030 World Cup.

Carrick took Man United training on Tuesday and has again been at Carrington on Wednesday amid the uncertainty surrounding his future.

At this stage, no confirmation has arrived in terms of a change of head coach, but the expectation is that the Englishman will lose his job over the next 24 hours or so.

Pochettino, who has previously managed Southampton, Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea in the Premier League, is said to be incredibly keen on the Man United job.

The Argentine's first game in charge of the 20-time English champions is set to be the trip to Anfield to tackle Liverpool in the Premier League on November 22.

Rangers manager Derek McInnes heaped praise on Ryan Naderi after the Czech added another goal to his tally in the 2-0 win over St Mirren – but insisted there is still far more to come from his in-form striker.

The 23-year-old stepped up to slot home a first-half penalty to take his total to nine for the season in all competitions, with skipper Dan Neil adding a second shortly after the hour-mark to seal a valuable three points on the road.

The result moves McInnes’ men to within a point of Premiership leaders Celtic – who take on Kilmarnock this afternoon – ahead of the international break.

And the manager was delighted with the way in which his frontman shrugged off an earlier miss to take responsibility for the spot-kick which set Rangers on their way in what was a potential banana-skin encounter in Paisley.

‘His first port of call is to make sure he’s a handful to play against and I thought he was that,’ said McInnes. ‘I thought he ran the gaps, he made sure every one of their centre-backs knew he was there, which is very important.

‘He needs to build that reputation for being horrible to play against, but equally at a club like Rangers you’re going to get judged on the goals.

Rangers boss Derek McInnes (pictured) is thrilled with Ryan Naderi's performances

The Czech striker (left) celebrates with Kim Min-su after breaking the deadlock in Paisley

‘If you’re going to lead the line for us, then getting those goals is so important and thankfully with his stats he’s really contributing.

‘He’s probably a bit annoyed he never added to it, but I thought he was terrific.

‘You can’t be unsure, you can’t be thinking, “Do I belong here?”.

‘I think he’s totally shown that he’s somebody you can depend on, somebody that can be trusted, somebody that you can rely on to get goals as well as bring in good performances.’

Rangers are now unbeaten in their last 12, but although McInnes is pleased with his side’s progress after a sticky start to the season, he is under no illusions that there is much to improve on.

‘That type of form gets you close to where you want to get to,’ he said. ‘There’s still loads of work to do and loads of improvements in the team, as you can see.

‘If we take our chances, we take the game away from St Mirren and while it’s still 1-0, they are always going to keep going.

#1811. GdS: The full story of Milan and Inter’s record-breaking €650m deal with Generali

More details continue to emerge regarding the stadium naming rights deal between AC Milan, Inter and Generali.

La Gazzetta dello Sport write that even before it’s even been built, the new home of Milan and Inter is already the place to be. It’s no coincidence that Generali – the insurance giant – has decided to put its stamp on the façades, as was revealed last month at the presentation of the stadium.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The collaboration kicks off immediately. Generali are now the Official Insurance Partner of the two clubs. The stadium naming rights contract will last for 25 years and includes the payment of €50m until the stadium opens in 2031.

This includes €10m annually for each of the next five seasons, including the current one, to be split equally between Inter and Milan. Once the stadium is inaugurated, the sum will increase to €30m annually (€15m each) for the following 20 years. The total commitment amounts to €650m.

Generali wanted to associate its name with the stadium from the very beginning of this long journey, in order to establish itself in the collective imagination: it will only be the Generali Stadium, with no temporary or secondary names to muddy the waters.

Branding a stadium from day one – or rather, even before it opens – is particularly strategic in terms of marketing. For this reason, Generali have agreed to pay €10m a year for something that, for five years, will be on models and then on construction sites, but not yet in the experience of fans.

Moreover, the naming rights market still has ample room for development in Europe. A Kroll study of the 36 major European clubs highlighted this already in 2024: only 12 had sold the naming rights to their stadiums, for a total estimated potential value of €303m, equivalent to an average of €8.4m per season.

Italy and England were the leagues least inclined to this form of commercialisation, also held back by the historical connection between the stadiums and their names. In this scenario, the new Inter and Milan stadium represents a different opportunity: a stadium to be built around a commercial identity,.

It’s not just a sports sponsorship: it’s a key support for a project crucial to the next stage of development of the city, the beating heart of the country’s economy and finances. This explains the significant investment.

It was the first time Inter and Milan worked together on the same side of the table, to secure a commercial deal. Under the watchful eye of Oaktree and RedBird Capital, the two clubs’ Chief Revenue Officers – Giorgio Ricci and Maikel Oettle – took the lead in finalising the sale of the naming rights.

These will be transferred through Stadio San Siro, a company controlled by NSM Holding, equally owned by Milan and Inter. The Rossoneri and Nerazzurri had initially selected a small group of potential partners, focusing on major Italian companies.

This type of right is particularly attractive to companies with a strong interest in the local area. After an initial round of meetings, Generali was the company that immediately showed the most enthusiasm.

Inter and AC Milan thus decided to further discuss the deal with the insurance giant, finalising the contract within a few months, the largest ever signed by Generali in the sports sector. In addition to the price offered, a key factor was the partner’s status.

Who better than the insurance giant – with €4.3bn in net profit and €900bn in assets under management – can offer guarantees of solidity and solvency, especially in a long-term commitment?

The €650m is written in stone and represents a significant portion of the financial coverage for the entire real estate transaction. Moreover, thanks to the €50m ‘bridge’ payment, the clubs have the opportunity to cash in immediately.

A comparison with other major international stadiums further illustrates the scale of the operation. Once fully operational, with €30m annually, the Generali Stadium will rank at the top of the global naming rights market, becoming one of the most lucrative deals ever signed for a stadium.

In Europe, the benchmark is Spotify’s Camp Nou, which guarantees Barcelona €20m per season, while Bayern Munich earn around €13m annually from Allianz for the Munich Arena. London’s Emirates Stadium is currently worth an estimated €10-15m to Arsenal.

Atletico Madrid’s Riyadh Air Metropolitano is at a similar level to that of the Gunners. In Germany, Borussia Dortmund get around €11m for Signal Iduna Park. Juventus, with the Allianz Stadium, earns around €8-10m.

To find higher figures, one must look primarily to the United States, where the stadium sponsorship market is of a different size and characteristics. The Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles is worth approximately €31m annually, but the $700m twenty-year contract also includes other commercial activities of the AEG group and partnerships with the Lakers and Kings.

The same is true for SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles, whose twenty-year, $625m agreement equates to approximately €28m annually, but includes additional commercial components. Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas, on the other hand, has signed a thirty-year agreement worth approximately $750m, equivalent to approximately €22m per season.

These transactions should be interpreted with caution, as the consideration does not always refer solely to the naming of the stadium. The Milan figure, however, is significant precisely because of the size of the naming rights component.

There is also another aspect to consider. The €30m guaranteed by Generali could represent only the first step in a much broader commercial strategy. An ecosystem of partnerships will develop around the new stadium, from technology services to beverage supplies, and other product categories that can be accommodated in the facility.

The goal is to raise an additional €20-25 million through agreements with secondary sponsors, bringing the overall value of the stadium’s commercial partnerships to even higher levels. Meanwhile, the market is also starting to move in Italy, albeit on a much smaller scale.

Atalanta earn approximately €2.5m annually from its partnership with New Balance for the naming of the New Balance Arena, while Udinese earns approximately €1m Bluenergy for the Bluenergy Stadium.

In short, the Milan deal risks rewriting the industry benchmarks, pushing up the valuations of other European venues and confirming how the name of a stadium, when associated with an international project, is a valuable asset.could become a top-level commercial asset.

#1809. International break dates 2027: Full calendar for next year

By Axel Clody | 11 Nov 2026 12:40

With a few fans and many critics, the FIFA international break will keep its reserved place in 2027, even without the biggest tournaments for Europeans and South Americans.

Next year maintains the new trend of 2026, which removed one of the breaks for international matches to create a longer period in which four matches can be accommodated instead of two.

Four dates will be set aside for international fixtures, one of them lasting 16 days, called the ‘Super FIFA Window’. All the others will last nine days, as usual. Brazilian football, however, will have one more because of the Women’s World Cup in the middle of the year.

22-30 March 7-15 June 20 September-5 October 8-16 November

The first FIFA window, in the third month of 2027, will feature several decisive fixtures around the world.

In Europe, the quarter-finals of the Nations League will be played, as will the Concacaf edition for the teams of North and Central America. The teams that are eliminated should look for friendlies against South American teams, as in June.

Also in March, Asian teams will begin qualifying for the 2030 World Cup and the 2031 Asian Cup. In Africa, the teams qualifying for the Africa Cup of Nations, which will be played in the middle of the year, when the Concacaf Gold Cup also takes place, will be decided.

The June FIFA window should be almost entirely friendlies, with the exception of the Nations League finals.

In September, South American World Cup qualifiers are expected to begin, although this has not yet been confirmed, and would also occupy the calendar in November. In Europe, countries will play qualification for Euro 2028.

Outside the FIFA windows, there will also be the 2027 Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia, which was scheduled for the start of the year but was postponed to be played between 23 December and 21 January 2028 because of conflicts in the Middle East. European clubs, which will be in the middle of next season, will be affected by the absence of players who will be at the tournament.

England’s calendar in 2027 will be shaped by the Nations League and qualifying for Euro 2028. Thomas Tuchel’s side are in Group A3 with Spain, Croatia and Czechia, and the group winner will go through to the quarter-finals in March 2027.

England still have two group games to play, against Croatia at Wembley on 12 November and away to Spain on 15 November. The Nations League finals are scheduled for 9-13 June 2027, with the host nation yet to be confirmed.

Euro 2028 will be played in the United Kingdom and Ireland from 9 June to 9 July 2028. The qualifying draw takes place in Belfast on 6 December 2026, with fixtures running from March to November 2027 and play-offs in March 2028. As co-hosts, England must still qualify, although UEFA has reserved two automatic places for host nations.

2028: 20-28 March 29 May-6 June June/July: Copa America and European Championship 18 September-3 October 13-21 November

2029: 19-27 March 4-12 June 29 September-9 October 12-20 November

2030: 18-26 March 3-11 June June/July: World Cup 23 September-8 October 11-19 November

Thomas Tuchel has revealed he has no release clause in his England contract but insists he will not follow after Mauricio Pochettino and leave international football mid-contract to take a high-profile club role.

Pochettino is midway through his deal as head coach of the United States but is ready to become Michael Carrick’s replacement as Manchester United manager.

Tuchel, however, maintains there is no job that would take him away from England before they contest Euro 2028 on home soil.

The England job is the first time Tuchel has managed within international football. He previously held four of Europe’s most prestigious club roles as head coach of Borussia Dortmund, Paris Saint-Germain, Chelsea and then Bayern Munich.

Pochettino only recently extended his United States contract to 2030 but is now ready to leave his post and head back into club football.

“No release clause and there’s no intention,” the German said when asked about his own situation.

“I signed a contract, I want to stay until the Euros. I want to do the Euros. We have unfinished business.”

When asked whether there was ‘zero chance’ of him leaving if a big club came in before Euro 2028, Tuchel said: “I would say so.”

Tuchel remains unwilling to discuss his longer-term future beyond the expiry of his contract but says he is “open for everything”. The 53-year-old added: “I’m in a good place, and I love the players.”

Referring to the months of the year without international football, he said: “I miss my players, and I miss my team, and I miss the 50 [club] matches that I’m not involved in a year.

#1807. Carrick sacked by Man Utd with Pochettino appointment expected

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Michael Carrick has been sacked as Manchester United's head coach, with Mauricio Pochettino expected to replace him.

Rumours had been rife that Carrick may be replaced during the international break, after a dreadful start to the season left United 18th in the Premier League table.

Despite fighting back from 2-0 and 4-2 down to draw 4-4 with Aston Villa on Sunday – the first time any team had recovered from two goals behind to equalise on two occasions in a single Premier League match – United are guaranteed to spend at least 15 days in the relegation zone.

It will be their longest run of successive days inside the drop zone since September and October 1986, when they endured a spell of 26 days in the First Division's danger zone.

That was also the last time United were in a worse position in the table at least 10 games into a season, having sat 20th on that occasion.

Back then, Ron Atkinson was dismissed in November, with Alex Ferguson taking the reins and spending 27 glittering years at the club.

Antonio Conte, Julian Nagelsmann and Eddie Howe had all been touted as possible replacements this time around, with the Red Devils seeking their third permanent boss since Jim Ratcliffe and INEOS took control of the club's football operations in February 2024.

However, United States boss Pochettino is widely expected to be announced as Carrick's successor.

15 – Manchester United are now guaranteed to spend at least 15 consecutive days in the Premier League relegation zone. It is their longest run of days in the top-flight drop zone since September/October 1986 (28). Dejected. https://t.co/wtpy0nCLOx

A club statement read: "After a disappointing start to the season, the club has come to the extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary in order to achieve our ambitions.

"Michael is, and always will be, a Manchester United legend. Just as he did as a player, he has conducted himself with the highest standards of dedication and professionalism throughout his time back with the club. His leadership and achievements last season will always be fondly remembered.

"The club intends to appoint a permanent successor as quickly as possible."

Carrick initially had a hugely positive impact upon replacing Ruben Amorim on an interim basis in January.

He led United to a third-place finish in the Premier League last season, winning 12 of his 17 games at the helm in 2025-26 (70%, D3 L2). The Red Devils also averaged 1.94 goals per game in that span, while conceding 1.05.

Having made Carrick their permanent boss on a two-year contract this summer, United have won three of 15 games in all competitions in 2026-27 (20%, D5 L5), averaging 1.6 goals for and exactly 2.0 goals against per match.

Their 30 goals conceded across all competitions are the joint-second most among all teams in Europe's top five leagues, with only Ligue 1 side Lens shipping more (31, also 30 conceded by Crystal Palace, Sassuolo and Getafe).

United have failed to keep a clean sheet in 10 Premier League games this term, with their only victory coming by a 5-2 scoreline against newly promoted Ipswich Town in August, failing to win any of their subsequent eight matches (D5 L3).

It is the first time they have started a campaign without a shutout in their first 10 matches since that 1986-97 season, while they are the first top-flight team to start a season with such a run, after finishing in the top three the previous campaign, since Liverpool in 1966-67.

Old Trafford was the scene of protests against the way INEOS and the Glazer family have run the club on Sunday, with United's players also attracting fierce criticism from their own supporters throughout the campaign.

Following a 3-0 defeat at home to Bournemouth last month, large sections of the Red Devils' fanbase applauded Carrick down the tunnel, before booing his players off.

Carrick, who previously had a short-lived spell as United's caretaker boss back in 2021, ended his second stint in the Old Trafford dugout with a 47% win rate, which is actually the highest of any permanent boss in the INEOS era, ahead of Erik ten Hag's 35% and Amorim's 38%.

United travel to Anfield to face old rivals Liverpool on November 22. A trip to Sporting CP in the Champions League follows three days later, with the Red Devils having six points on the board in that competition, after four matches.

#1804. Non-league footballer in stable condition after collapsing in warm-up and being rushed to hospital, leading to match being abandoned

By BEN WILLCOCKS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 11:35 EST, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 19:08 EST, 7 November 2026

Truro City's match against Folkestone Invicta was abandoned due to a medical emergency on Saturday after a footballer collapsed during the warm-up.

Yassine En-Neyah, 26, was rushed to hospital in an ambulance after collapsing while preparing with his team-mates on the pitch. It was later confirmed he was in a stable condition.

The former Nottingham Forest academy youngster had been named among the substitutes to face Folkestone in the National League South game in Kent.

A club statement on Saturday read: 'Truro City can confirm that this afternoon's match against Folkestone Invicta has been postponed.

'Yassine En-Neyah required medical assistance during the warm-up and was transferred to the William Harvey hospital in Ashford for further treatment.'

The club added a welcome on Saturday night, saying: 'He is stable, sitting up and chatting, but will remain in hospital overnight under observation.

Truro City's clash with Folkestone Invicta has been abandoned due to a medical emergency

Yassine En-Neyah - pictured before the game - was named on the bench to face Folkestone

Club Statement:Truro City can confirm that this afternoon's match against Folkestone Invicta has been postponed. Yassine En-Neyah required medical assistance during the warm-up and was transferred to the William Harvey hospital in Ashford for further treatment.We will… pic.twitter.com/IyiF2VIFMz

'The club would like to place on record its thanks to Truro City's medical staff, their counterparts at Folkestone Invicta, along with all club personnel from the home club.

'Both the National League and Football Association have also offered their help and support. There have also been many well wishes from Truro City fans and the wider football community too.'

Truro City's players had earlier gathered around the rear of the ambulance where En-Neyah was being treated to shield him from view.

The Moroccan-born former Republic of Ireland youth international began his career at Nottingham Forest, making his professional debut in January 2020 as a substitute during an FA Cup third-round clash against Chelsea.

After being released by Forest in 2021, the winger has played for multiple non-league sides including Shelbourne, Waterford and Maldon & Tipree.

Having briefly represented Truro in 2023, En-Neyah returned to the Tinners for a second spell in 2024, where he has remained since.

When he signed his new Truro contract last season, En-Neyah admitted he didn't think twice about the decision to stay.

'Truro's been my home for the last couple of seasons and it was a very easy decision,' he told BBC Radio Cornwall.

'I feel home so I just want to continue working hard and help the club achieve greater things.

'It wasn't a case of having to think about it, it was just a matter of getting it done and continuing to work hard and do well for the club and for myself.'

#1803. Scotland vs North Macedonia - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ellis Stevens | 11 Nov 2026 12:43

Scotland and North Macedonia will clash at Hampden Park on Friday night in UEFA Nations League B Group 1.

The hosts are third in the standings with four points, while the visitors are bottom of the table and yet to pick up a single point from four matches.

Since replacing long-serving manager Steve Clarke, who stepped down at the end of a disappointing 2026 World Cup campaign, new boss Sebastian Pocognoli has endured a mixed start to life in charge.

Pocognoli has guided Scotland to just one win from four Nations League fixtures, beating Friday's visitors 2-1, alongside a 0-0 draw with Slovenia, a 3-0 defeat to Switzerland and, most recently, a 2-1 defeat against Slovenia.

Scotland, as a result, sit third in League B Group 1 with four points, leaving them four points above bottom-placed North Macedonia and three points behind second-placed Slovenia in the promotion-playoff place, while leaders Switzerland are out of reach with only two games remaining.

With Scotland hoping to secure a second-placed finish and promotion playoff place, Pocognoli's side will be desperate to secure all three points on Friday to potentially move level with Slovenia, who face Switzerland.

Despite their struggles in the group campaign, including scoring only three goals across four matches, Scotland will draw confidence from their dominant 2-0 win in the reverse fixture against North Macedonia, when they took 25 shots and had seven big chances compared to their opponents' nine shots and zero big chances.

North Macedonia also head into Friday's encounter enduring a miserable five-game losing streak and 12-game winless run across all competitions.

Adding to their concerning form, North Macedonia have failed to score in 10 of those matches, including each of their last eight outings.

Goce Sedloski, who took charge in December 2025, is, therefore, still searching for his first win as North Macedonia manager, and he will be desperate to finally secure a victory on Friday.

The visitors will have to improve across all areas of the pitch if they are to secure any points, having failed to score and conceded 10 goals in their four Nations League games.

A victory will also be required for North Macedonia to have any chance of avoiding a relegation playoff match, with three points and at least a draw, with Scotland losing both remaining matches and a significant swing in goal difference, needed to climb to third.

Scotland are boosted by the return of Scott McTominay, who did not feature in the first four Nations League matches due to undergoing heart surgery.

The midfielder is expected to return straight into the starting 11, providing attacking support for Oli McBurnie, with John McGinn, Lewis Ferguson and Billy Gilmour featuring in midfield.

At the back, Aaron Hickey could start on the right of a back-three, alongside Jack Hendry and Luis Binks, while Ben Gannon-Doak and Andy Robertson provide width from wing-back.

As for North Macedonia, captain Enis Bardhi should start in attacking midfield, with Ljupche Doriev and Dimitar Mitrovski providing support from the wings for striker Elmin Rastoder.

Further back, Eljif Elmas and Jani Atanasov should start at the base of midfield, with Visar Misliu and Anes Meljichi starting in central defence.

Gunn; Hickey, Hendry, Binks; Doak, McGinn, Ferguson, Gilmour, Robertson; McTominay; McBurnie

North Macedonia possible starting lineup:

Dimitrievski; Ilievski, Meljichi, Misliu, Alioski; Elmas, Atanasov, Mitrovski, Bardhi, Doriev; Rastoder

Scotland may be enduring a difficult run, but they demonstrated their superiority over the struggling North Macedonia in the reverse fixture and should secure another comfortable win on Friday.

#1802. Crystal Palace sack Pierre Sage with Thomas Frank in advanced talks over job

Crystal Palace have sacked manager Pierre Sage, with Thomas Frank in advanced talks over becoming his replacement.

The Eagles have won just two Premier League matches all season and sit bottom of the Premier League table after a run of four consecutive defeats.

The 3-1 home loss to Liverpool on Sunday was ultimately the final straw for chairman Steve Parish and the club hierarchy, with Eddie Nketiah’s injury-time penalty a mere consolation on another dark day at Selhurst Park.

Palace have won just once in their last eight games across all competitions - in the Carabao Cup last 16 against fellow strugglers Fulham last month.

That dismal run of results included a 5-0 hammering at high-flying rivals Brighton, as well as a 2-0 defeat by Tottenham, albeit after Jean-Philippe Mateta’s early red card.

“Crystal Palace Football Club can confirm that Pierre Sage has left his role as Manager,” Palace said in an official statement on Thursday, shortly after Manchester United announced the sacking of Michael Carrick.

“Three members of Pierre’s coaching staff – Jamal Alioui, Damien Della Santa and Sandy Guichard – have also left the club.

“The club would like to place on record its thanks to Pierre and his staff for their efforts during their time in South London, and wish them well for the future.

“An update on the process of appointing a new Manager will be provided in due course.”

Former Spurs and Brentford boss Frank is the frontrunner to take over from Sage, in what would be a first foray back into management since his sacking by Tottenham back in February, when he was dismissed after only eight months at the helm and two wins in 17 games.

Palace only appointed Sage on a three-year contract in June to replace Oliver Glasner, who won the FA Cup, Community Shield and Conference League during a memorable two-and-a-half year spell in south London before leaving at the end of last season following the expiration of his deal and eventually joining Nottingham Forest.

Sage - who previously managed Lyon - left Lens for Selhurst Park after a year in charge that saw him deliver the first Coupe de France success in the club’s history and a second-place finish in Ligue 1 behind reigning champions Paris Saint-Germain, earning him manager of the year honours in the French top-flight.

Former Tottenham and Chelsea boss Pochettino has been sounded out as INEOS’ preferred candidate, ahead of other potential options that were previously reported, like Eddie Howe, Antonio Conte and Julian Nagelsmann.

The Argentine is currently the head coach of the United States, but it was reported by BBC Sport that United were willing to trigger the £7million clause in his contract with US Soccer to bring him to Old Trafford.

It is believed that there is an agreement in principle between United and Pochettino for the 54-year-old to take over the reins from Carrick, but there has been no official indication as of yet.

BBC Sport claims that Pochettino is likely to take up his post by November 19 at the latest, but there remains a level of uncertainty as to whether he will manage the US’ two matches against Panama in the current international break.

The United hierarchy had identified this international window as a chance to assess Carrick’s position as manager, and they pulled the trigger after days of leaked reporting claiming that the ex-England international was to be relieved of his duties following a crisis meeting in Monaco on Wednesday.

By Darren Plant | 11 Nov 2026 12:53

West Ham United and Atletico Madrid have allegedly joined the race to sign River Plate goalkeeper Santiago Beltran.

Meanwhile, Atletico Madrid's defeat to Barcelona last weekend has left Diego Simeone's side as outsiders in the La Liga title race.

Therefore, it is plausible that both clubs will be in the market for new players in 2027, including the winter transfer window.

Although he has conceded just 36 goals and kept 19 clean sheets in 45 matches, the one-cap Argentina international's contract is due to expire in December 2027.

As a result, River Plate are seemingly eager to find a buyer in January, with Beltran expected to move to Europe.

#1798. Kane ranks 126th cap among his biggest England moments

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Harry Kane says winning his 126th cap and becoming England's all-time leading appearance-maker will rank among the greatest moments of his career.

England face Croatia in their penultimate group-stage match in the Nations League on Thursday, with head coach Thomas Tuchel already confirming Kane will start the game.

That will take Kane to 126 senior appearances for the Three Lions, surpassing Peter Shilton (125) outright to become the most-capped player in the team's history.

With 91 goals, Kane is already the most prolific player in England's history by some margin, having passed Wayne Rooney's previous record of 53 goals over three years ago.

Since making his England debut in 2015, Kane has put together a case to be the greatest player to ever represent the Three Lions, helping them reach two European Championship finals and two World Cup semi-finals, one of which led to a bronze medal this year.

Ahead of his landmark outing, Kane will also have the honour of presenting the Ballon d'Or trophy to England's fans, having become his country's first winner of the award since Michael Owen in 2001.

Asked where the match will rank among his best England moments, Kane said: "It's definitely up there as the biggest. I think it showcases consistency at the highest level.

"It's testament to all the dedication, the time people don't see, that keeps me fit and healthy.

"This is one of the biggest milestones in my career. In terms of what's next, I don't like to set limits – 100 goals is a milestone to reach as soon as possible.

"We've done extremely well in tournaments, getting to the latter stages. I'm feeling really good and, hopefully, there will be many more years to see what I can achieve."

“It’s one of the biggest milestones of my career.”  The skipper himself on his record-breaking appearance for the #ThreeLions  https://t.co/FiEwBouest

Asked to name some of his other favourite moments in an England shirt, two matches from this year's World Cup immediately sprung to mind for Kane – a 2-1 comeback win over DR Congo in which he scored both goals, and a nail-biting 3-2 triumph over Mexico at the Estadio Azteca in the following round, when his penalty proved decisive.

He said: "The England debut is always a big one. That dream coming true, scoring at Wembley on my debut… coming on for Wayne Rooney will always stick in my mind.

"From the recent World Cup, the DR Congo game was just an incredible experience, to help the team get through a knockout game like that, to score the two goals. The second goal was one of my best finishes and just the feeling of adrenaline afterwards was as good as it gets.

"I've been lucky enough to have some great moments but the major tournament moments, like the Mexico game, they're the ones that really stick in the memory."

And Kane is very clear on what he still wants to accomplish at international level, as he aims to lead England to their first major trophy since the 1966 World Cup.

"To win a team trophy for England, a major trophy, is my biggest dream," Kane said. "A World Cup or the Euros, or both, hopefully, but I know how difficult that is.

"Individual accolades are incredible, but ultimately they're a consequence of trying to make the team better.

"With Bayern Munich, winning the Champions League [is the aim]. There are many trophies I haven't won and that's what motivates me. I'm surrounded by great teams at my club and country, so, hopefully, it's an exciting time ahead."

#1797. England vs Croatia: Prediction, kick-off time, TV, live stream, team news, h2h results, odds today

The Standard's journalism is supported by our readers. If you click links to other sites on this page, we will earn commission.

England face Croatia tonight in the penultimate game of the Nations League group stage, with captain Harry Kane to become their most-capped men’s player of all time.

Fresh from winning the Ballon d’Or in London last month, Kane is set to make his 126th senior international appearance on Thursday evening to move clear of long-time record-holder Peter Shilton.

Croatia head to Wembley with their mauling at the hands of the Three Lions in Rijeka last month still fresh in the memory.

Thomas Tuchel’s side put seven past their hosts without reply, as Kane and Bukayo Saka both bagged braces. There were further goals from Jude Bellingham, Anthony Gordon and Morgan Rogers in a match played technically behind closed doors, but with thousands of schoolchildren permitted to attend.

England are poised to advance to the next stage of the Nations League but currently via a second-placed finish, which would set up a quarter-final with a big hitter such as France or Portugal.

Victory for England at Wembley would likely tee up a mouthwatering last-game decider away in Spain on Sunday, with the winner of that match topping the group.

England vs Croatia is scheduled for a 7.45pm GMT kick-off tonight on Thursday November 12, 2026.

The match will take place at Wembley Stadium in north-west London.

TV channel: In the UK, England vs Croatia in the 2026/27 Nations League is being televised live and free to air on ITV, with coverage of the match beginning at 7pm on ITV1.

Live stream: Catch the game live online through the ITVX website and app, which is free with a registration.

Live blog: You can follow all the action with Standard Sport’s live blog, featuring expert insight and analysis from England correspondents Dom Smith and Sam Tabuteau.

Injuries to Marc Guehi, Djed Spence and Ezri Konsa have led to late England call-ups for Dan Burn and James Hill, with the latter hoping to make his senior debut.

Other potential debutants include Fulham's Josh King and Borussia Dortmund midfielder Jobe Bellingham, younger brother of England star Jude Bellingham.

England are a bit light on the right flank with Arsenal duo Saka and Noni Madueke both not in the squad, with Chelsea’s Rogers or Liverpool youngster Rio Ngumoha likely to start instead.

For Croatia, ex-Tottenham winger Ivan Perisic is suspended after his red card last time out against Spain in Split.

After last month’s chastening 7-0 loss to England, many in Croatia are writing this game off, with calls to rest legendary 41-year-old Luka Modric for the crunch clash with the Czech Republic on Sunday.

As mentioned above, this fixture has already produced plenty of goals. Croatia have been leaky at the back throughout the Nations League campaign, conceding 14 times in four games.

Where to watch England vs Croatia: TV channel and live stream

A 4-1 drubbing at the hands of Spain in their last away match indicates that England should have plenty of chances to score at home.

While the Three Lions were able to keep Croatia quiet in Rijeka, their guests on Thursday night usually score at least once. It would not be a surprise to see England match Spain’s latest result against Croatia.

England and Croatia have crossed paths in three of the last four major tournaments, with the Three Lions victorious on two occasions. However, Croatia had the last laugh - beating England in the semi-finals of the World Cup in Russia in 2018.

Overall, this is a fixture England usually win - but Croatia have inflicted major upsets before, preventing England from qualifying for Euro 2008 with wins home and away.

#1796. Man City's slump cannot be excused by guilty verdict: Too many blunders, too much arm waving and football problems are piling up after 3-1 defeat by Nottingham Forest, writes JACK GAUGHAN

Published: 14:52 EST, 7 November 2026 | Updated: 19:21 EST, 7 November 2026

This run will not be about the verdicts. This cannot be about the verdicts. Footballers do not care about these things, the stuff out of their control. Besides, all of them are earning cut-price transfers elsewhere were Manchester City to suffer relegation anyway. And cut-price fees mean bulkier salaries.

So to them the current climate, the circumstances around City – their recent history and their immediate future – does not overly matter. Sure, there might be the odd one who is slightly more philosophical and inquisitive about appeals and appendices but the majority won't be giving it much or any thought.

City insist on their innocence publicly and privately; until that changes, their players and Enzo Maresca carry on regardless. There were the usual jeers here, there were ditties about cheating, but that surely cannot affect them.

Instead, the performances over the past few weeks, this a third consecutive Premier League defeat and now sinking six points adrift of Arsenal, cannot be excused by the findings of an independent commission. The problems are football problems.

This is a squad who appear uncertain about specific aspects of their game. Namely how to build from the back – and that is prompting individual mistakes. It happened against Ipswich Town and at Aston Villa. On the river Trent, it was no different.

The statistics say City dominated another game and they deserved more but the eyes tell another story.

Man City are a squad who now appear uncertain about specific aspects of their game

The statistics say City dominated another game and they deserved more but the eyes tell another story

Three defeats in a row have seen Enzo Maresca's side slip six points behind leaders Arsenal

Too many errors. Too much arm waving. Too much feeling sorry for themselves when decisions go elsewhere. Oliver Glasner is not stupid, he will have seen examples of this play out in parts of City's victories as well as reverses.

As Liam Delap raced into the corner to celebrate his second with 17 minutes left – a huge day in his career against the club which moulded him – Glasner was dashing down the touchline with unbridled joy.

Nottingham Forest (5-2-2-1): Sels 6; Munoz 6 (Netz 65, 6), Cunha 8, Milenkovic 8, Murillo 7, Williams 8; Yates 8 (Sangare 79), Schlager 8; McAtee 7 (Ndoye 65, 6), Gibbs-White 7; Delap 9 (Jesus 87)

Man City (4-1-4-1): Donnarumma 5; Khusanov 5, Dias 5, Guehi 4 (Nunes 46, 7), Gvardiol 4 (O'Reilly 46, 6); Anderson 5; Ndiaye 6, Cherki 6, Fernandez 4 (Foden 78), Doku 6; Haaland 5

Forest displays have deserved more than their points total so far and this was vindication for their fifth manager in 14 months, who suggested he fancied sampling Nottingham’s nightlife afterwards. Delap was exceptional, some personal redemption after criticism.

The way in which Glasner nudged James McAtee further forward, stationed higher from the off in order to pressurise the visitors, spoke to an idea that City arrived here ready to be ruffled and have been wearing a look of fragility.

By the time this was eight minutes shy of half time and McAtee was nicking possession from Elliot Anderson, drawing a foul that sparked another onslaught on Gianluigi Donnarumma's box, Forest were already two clear – and had been for some time. Phil Foden warmed up on the touchline, laughing and hugging with Callum Hudson-Odoi.

Forest preyed on City insecurities. A midfield structure that is simply not working at the moment, easily railroaded. A defence allergic to the basics and an epidemic of individual mistakes – either as a result of nervousness or blase attitude on the ball.

Straight to the mistakes. A real collection, these: the first in the fifth minute and the others 13 minutes afterwards. Jair Cunha wheeled away after picking Josko Gvardiol's pocket, meandering forward into the box and side-footing into the far corner largely unchallenged. Gvardiol seemed to have the air of a man who felt invincible when gathering possession before being eased off it.

Later, as Delap thundered forward 45 yards unchecked to hammer past Donnarumma, you wondered about the communication between these City players. Anderson and Iliman Ndiaye left things to each other near halfway, Xaver Schlager gave his thanks – finding Delap – and the City academy graduate bulldozed clear. Marc Guehi waved him through, Ruben Dias dithered and Maresca bowed his head.

Liam Delap was exceptional for Nottingham Forest, some personal redemption after criticism

Remarkably, this was the first time in seven years that City had gone two down inside 18 minutes

Remarkably, this was the first time in seven years that City had gone two down inside 18 minutes. Dias looked aghast at Guehi, who was then hooked at the break alongside Gvardiol. Erling Haaland and Rayan Cherki both stood in the centre circle, hands on hips.

It later emerged via replays that Anderson had been arguing with Abdukodir Khusanov in the build-up to Forest's opener as well, proof that City were nowhere near close to producing what was expected when on the ball in their own half.

Glasner had the weapons at his disposal to make this work but even the Austrian must have been surprised at the way in which they tickled City's soft underbelly. They had not scored at the City Ground all season. All change when owner Evangelos Marinakis made his first trip to see a game since Glasner's appointment, which felt particularly handy, with Yates having delivered a spinetingling dressing room speech pre-match.

Anger permeated the eyes of some City players as the whistle went. Cherki stormed down the tunnel, animatedly discussing how to play through Forest with Fernandez when they re-emerged.

Their lifeline came after 52 minutes, a Ryan Yates deflection from Jeremy Doku's cross sitting up for Cherki to hammer home a half-volley off the bar. Doku soon almost squeezed another effort past Matz Sels and the mood shifted, City briefly creeping menacingly like the monsters they are portrayed as.

Maresca had introduced Matheus Nunes and Nico O'Reilly, with both affecting the upturn. An admission of selection errors, perhaps, although O'Reilly is managing an ongoing back issue and is set for therapy on it over the international break.

City will need some of that as a collective. Delap won the ball inside his own third, gliding past Anderson, and Forest's explosive counter ended with Delap spearing a shot in off the post after Morgan Gibbs-White carried possession unopposed for 60 yards. Delirium, Glasner darting to the corner flag.

The quirk of this is that City's failings mean Manchester United drop into the bottom three.

Maresca criticised Manchester City’s lack of fight but insisted that City created enough chances to leave with something despite admitting his players were physically second best.

‘In the first half we were not good enough - we didn't match the intensity that these kind of games require,’ Maresca said.

‘If you are not able to win the second balls then you struggle. You have to match the desire to win second balls and duels, otherwise it is not good. When you lost balls the way we did and cannot recover immediately, it’s a matter of winning duels.’

Maresca has a two-week international break to rake over the issues affecting his side and believes time away could do the squad good.

The Italian added: ‘When you lose a game you always want to go again immediately to try to win games but I think that this international break, the last one until March, is also good for the players.

‘We didn't match the intensity. We need to understand the reason why and try to avoid the next games. There is no panic. We need to understand but no panic.’

Maresca revealed that defenders Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol asked to come off at half time with injuries, while Forest out-ran his team by 6km on the night.

‘If you want to win against City, you need to do this,’ Oliver Glasner said after recording his first home win. ‘Credit to Liam, these strikes are something you have or you don't have.

‘It can be a turning point but we have to prove it. The way we performed today should give us confidence.’

City winger Jeremy Doku could not explain why they could not deal with Forest before half time.

‘We are used to playing every two days - that's not a reason,’ Doku said. ‘If you ask me for the reason for our first half I don't know.

‘We reacted too late. We need to be fresh minds, start again and analyse what we can do better and move forward. The international break comes at the right moment for us to analyse and come back refreshed.’

#1795. Manchester United: Biggest winners and losers from Mauricio Pochettino move revealed

Mauricio Pochettino looks set to succeed Michael Carrick as Manchester United manager.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea boss currently manages the USA national team and is expected to stay in post for their upcoming two-legged Concacaf Nations League quarter-final tie against Haiti.

United, though, will push ahead with negotiations for Pochettino after confirming Carrick’s sacking on Thursday and are expected to have him in place ahead of next weekend’s trip to Liverpool.

Pochettino will have a huge task on his hands should he take the reins, with United in the relegation zone and without a Premier League win since August.

Their squad, a mismatch of profiles and tactical fits from different managers, is also in desperate need of an overhaul, and Pochettino, with his own strictly defined style, will have ideas about who he wants to keep and who will be shown the door.

With that in mind, Standard Sport has identified the potential winners and losers from Pochettino’s imminent appointment at Old Trafford.

Despite playing an important role in United’s resurgence towards the end of last season, Patrick Dorgu has found his minutes restricted this term.

When Pochettino will take over Man Utd as ‘start date revealed’

Tuchel issues England future latest as Pochettino set for Man Utd

Angry Man Utd fans react to Carrick sacking as new statement sent

Discover a hidden island paradise in the Indian Ocean

The 22-year-old is an exciting attacking outlet but has increasingly earned a reputation as a defensive liability.

That, coupled with a hamstring injury, saw him fall out of favour under Carrick, but there could be an opportunity for the Danish left-back if Pochettino is appointed.

Pochettino has tended to deploy explosive attacking full-backs during his managerial career, and Dorgu’s physicality and instinctive attacking movement make him an unpredictable presence in the final third.

Dorgu is a raw but talented player, and Pochettino might enjoy the challenge of moulding him into a more rounded full-back while still utilising his attacking capabilities.

Massively underutilised since his breakthrough season under Erik ten Hag, Kobbie Mainoo is the sort of young, mobile presence Pochettino would be looking for in midfield.

The epicentre of Pochettino’s Spurs side was Mousa Dembele, who was lauded for his ability to withstand pressure and carry the ball from deep.

Those are attributes Mainoo has in abundance, and while his minutes have been limited over the last few seasons, his ability is not in question, and he would surely benefit from Pochettino’s nurturing personality.

In the absence of Mainoo and the injured Carlos Baleba, Man Utd’s midfield lacks pace, mobility and ingenuity.

That is a problem Pochettino will be keen to fix straight away, and he would be best served by reintegrating Mainoo rather than looking to the transfer market for solutions.

Mateus Cunha has a difficult profile to nail down, and that makes him a problem for defenders but also an issue for whoever is tasked with fitting him into their tactical setup.

Not quite a striker and not quite a No10, Cunha has shown glimpses of his quality at United and has the intensity and character to deliver under pressure.

His inconsistency is what lets him down at times, though, and he needs a manager who plays to his strengths and allows him the freedom to drift fluidly across the frontline.

Pochettino could be that coach, having played a pivotal role in developing Dele Alli into a uniquely talented player at Tottenham.

Dele was not just a goalscorer, but a ball carrier, creator and link man that got the best out of Harry Kane.

Cunha has the talent to be all those things for United. He just needs the guidance of a manager such as Pochettino to realise his ability.

Luke Shaw may have been given his break under Pochettino when the pair were at Southampton, but 14 years after first coming to prominence, the game has moved on.

Shaw, for all his talent, has been broken by injuries and simply can’t be relied upon to perform the responsibilities Pochettino needs from his full-backs.

United have been patient with Shaw, as his body has let him down time and time again, but it is now best for all parties if he moves on at the end of his contract.

If United are to get Pochettino’s appointment right, then they simply have to make these sorts of ruthless decisions.

Another player who should have left United years ago. Harry Maguire is a strong leader and a resilient character, but he simply is not and has not been good enough for United.

The 33-year-old should take some credit for how he saved his United career after being booed relentlessly by his own fans, but given the club’s situation, there is no space for sentimentality, and Pochettino would be wise to inform Maguire to look for a move away.

In Leny Yoro and Matthijs de Ligt, fitness permitting, United have two centre-backs who complement each other well and have enough years ahead of them to form a partnership under Pochettino.

Despite only arriving at the club over the summer, Youri Tielemans has struggled with the step up at United and has routinely been exposed for his lack of mobility.

A talented ball player, Tielemans’ best attributes are not particularly well suited to the style Pochettino likes to play, and he could be moved aside as United search for more pace and energy in the middle of the park.

With everyone fit and available, Mainoo and Baleba feel like the most complete midfield pairing United have at their disposal.

Tielemans, meanwhile, is an unorthodox fit for a team that lacks an identity in possession and will likely resort to a high-energy, transitional style in the first few weeks and months post-Carrick.
